FLEX LTD.

SUPPLEMENT TO PROXY STATEMENT DATED OCTOBER 5, 2026

FOR THE EXTRAORDINARY GENERAL MEETING OF SHAREHOLDERS

TO BE HELD ON NOVEMBER 2, 2026

On October 5, 2026, Flex Ltd. (the “Company”) filed a definitive proxy statement (the “Proxy Statement”) with the Securities and Exchange Commission in connection with the Company’s Extraordinary General Meeting of Shareholders to be held on November 2, 2026. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein have their respective meanings set forth in the Proxy Statement, except as noted below.

In connection with Proposal No. 2 of the Proxy Statement, the Company is filing this supplement (this “Supplement”) to the Proxy Statement to include the forms of the Guadalajara Leases and the Guadalajara Site Services Agreements (each as defined below), and the Existing Warrant, the Warrant Amendment and the form of Spinco Warrant (each as defined below), as Annexes U, V, W, X and Y to the Proxy Statement. The name of the Warrantholder before the Warrant Amendment is corrected to be Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC.

In connection with the separation and distribution, certain Spinco and Flex subsidiaries expect to enter into two long-term lease agreements pursuant to which the applicable Flex subsidiaries will continue to occupy certain buildings and related areas at the Guadalajara, Mexico campus following the Distribution (collectively, the “Guadalajara Leases”), and Spinco and/or certain of its subsidiaries intend to enter into two site services agreements with Flex and/or certain of its subsidiaries governing the provision of certain facility, utility and other site-based services pursuant to service level agreements at the Guadalajara, Mexico campus following the Distribution (collectively, the “Guadalajara Site Services Agreements”). The Guadalajara Leases are expected to address the leased premises, the term, rent and other charges, as well as access to and use of common areas and shared infrastructure and the parties’ respective maintenance and repair obligations. The forms of the Guadalajara Leases and the forms of the Guadalajara Site Services Agreements (including the service level agreements for power and water), each as may be modified or supplemented prior to the Distribution Date, are attached as Annex A and Annex B, respectively, to this Supplement.

Separately, on October 9, 2026, Flex, the Warrantholder and the Assignee entered into an amendment (the “Warrant Amendment”) to the Warrant (the “Existing Warrant”) which, as previously described in the Proxy Statement, provides that instead of Spinco shares, Spinco will issue to the Assignee a fully vested warrant to purchase Spinco shares at an exercise price of $0.01 per share (the “Spinco Warrant”). The full text of the Existing Warrant, the Warrant Amendment and the form of Spinco Warrant are attached as Annex C, D and E, respectively, to this Supplement.

This Supplement, including Annexes A, B, C, D and E, should be read in conjunction with the Proxy Statement. Except as described above, this Supplement does not amend, supplement or otherwise affect the Proxy Statement.

Annex A

LEASE AGREEMENT

(GUAD NORTH — Carretera Base Aérea, Zapopan, Jalisco, Mexico)

THIS LEASE AGREEMENT (this “Lease”) is entered into by and between PARQUE DE TECNOLOGÍA ELECTRÓNICA, S.A. DE C.V., a Mexican corporation (“Landlord”), and the Tenant named below, and is dated as of the Effective Date (as defined on the signature page).

BASIC LEASE INFORMATION

 

Tenant:    FLEXTRONICS PLASTICS, S.A. DE C.V. (“FPL” or “Tenant”), a Mexican corporation.
Related Lease:    The lease agreement of even date herewith between Landlord and FLEXTRONICS TECHNOLOGIES MEXICO, S. DE R.L. DE C.V. (“FTM”) in respect of Buildings 27, 29, 31 and 33 and thirty percent (30%) of Building 24 at the Site (the “FTM Lease”). This Lease and the FTM Lease are independent of each other: the obligations of Tenant and FTM are not joint and several, and no breach or default under either of them shall constitute a breach or default under the other. See Section 36(i).
Site:    The industrial campus known as Guad North, comprised of four (4) parcels totaling approximately 532,832 m², covered by public deeds Nos. 10,558, 42,464, 41,195 and 18,759, as legally described on Exhibit A-1 (each a “Parcel” and collectively, the “Site”).
Premises:    Buildings 3, 5 and 7, together with the Exclusive Areas and the right to use the Shared Areas, all as identified on the Site Plan attached as Exhibit A and as further described on Exhibit B (the “Premises”). Final areas per Exhibit B.
Commencement Date:    [•]
Lease Term:    Twenty-five (25) years from the Commencement Date (the “Primary Term”), being the maximum period permitted for real property devoted to industry under Article 2045 of the Civil Code of the State of Jalisco, subject to Tenant’s rights under Sections 4 and 24.
Base Rent:    U.S.$[•] per square foot of the Premises per calendar month, as set forth on Addendum 1. Denominated in U.S. Dollars, adjusted annually in accordance with Section 5(c).
Operating Expenses:    Borne by Landlord as provided in Section 7. Property tax (impuesto predial), insurance premiums and contributions for improvements (contribuciones de mejoras) are for Landlord’s account. This Lease is a gross lease, and no maintenance, repair, replacement or operating costs of the Site, the Shared Areas or the Premises shall be passed through to Tenant, as provided in Section 9(c).

Addenda:    1. Base Rent Schedule; 2. Extension Options and Year-25 Election; 3. [Intentionally Omitted]; 4. Usufruct Economics.

1. GRANTING CLAUSE; DELIVERY; CONDITION OF THE PREMISES

 

  (a)

In consideration of the obligation of Tenant to pay Rent as herein provided and of the other terms, covenants and conditions hereof, Landlord leases to Tenant, and Tenant takes from Landlord, the Premises, to have and to hold for the Lease Term, including (i) the exclusive right to use and occupy the Exclusive Areas, (ii) the non-exclusive right to use the Shared Areas in common with Landlord and the other occupants of the Site, and (iii) all easements, rights of way and appurtenances necessary or convenient for the use of the Premises for the Permitted Uses, including vehicular and pedestrian ingress and egress to and from the public roads serving the Site.

 

  (b)

Landlord shall not voluntarily grant any easement, right of way, restriction, covenant or other encumbrance, nor amend or terminate any existing one, that affects the Exclusive Areas or that would materially and adversely affect Tenant’s operations at the Premises or its access thereto, including through the Shared Areas or the access routes described on Exhibit C, without Tenant’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Tenant shall not voluntarily grant or create any easement, right of way, restriction, covenant or other encumbrance affecting the Premises, the Shared Areas or the Site, other than the subleases and occupancy rights permitted under Section 20, without Landlord’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

 

  (c)

Condition of the Premises. The Premises are existing, constructed and in operation, and Tenant takes them in their condition as of the Commencement Date, as inspected by Tenant, on an “as-is” basis, subject only to the following, which are conditions of delivery and not merely representations: (i) as of the Commencement Date, the Building systems and equipment serving the Premises (including electrical, mechanical, fire protection, HVAC, ventilation, water, sewer, compressed air, lighting, dock doors, dock levelers and elevators) shall be in good working order consistent with their operation immediately prior to the Commencement Date and in compliance with all Legal Requirements, except as otherwise recorded in the Baseline Condition Report; (ii) the Premises shall be free of any condition, other than as recorded in the Baseline Condition Report, that prevents, restricts or conditions the operation of Tenant’s business as conducted immediately prior to the Commencement Date; and (iii) Landlord and Tenant shall jointly prepare and execute, on the Commencement Date, a delivery and acceptance certificate (acta de entrega-recepción) and inventory of the Premises, and attach as Exhibit J a delivery condition report (the “Delivery Condition Report”) recording, as of the Commencement Date, the physical, environmental and regulatory compliance condition of the Premises (including urban development, environmental, civil protection, structural, permitting and licensing matters), the status of the Building systems, the meter readings and the keys handed over, the existing operating permits and licenses, the existing utility infrastructure and metering, and the outstanding regulatory matters listed on Exhibit G; and (iv) Landlord and Tenant shall jointly prepare, each Party bearing its own costs, no later than the Commencement Date, and the Parties shall attach as Exhibit K, (A) an inventory of the Site Equipment (as defined in Section 3(e)) located on, within, above or adjacent to the Buildings comprising the Premises, identifying for each item its owner, location, function, the Buildings or operations it serves, whether it is installed on a permanent or temporary basis, and any commitment previously made for its relocation or removal,

  it being acknowledged that Tenant and its Affiliates have operated such equipment prior to the Commencement Date and are familiar with it; Tenant shall, for that purpose, provide Landlord with the information in its possession regarding such equipment, including its maintenance records (and Landlord shall likewise provide Tenant with the information in its possession regarding the Site Equipment and the Premises, including maintenance records, manuals, warranties and Permits), and shall separately identify in the inventory any machinery, equipment or other property owned by Tenant, its Affiliates or its customers, which shall not constitute Site Equipment, shall remain the property of its owner, and shall be governed by Section 11(b), and (B) a baseline environmental report prepared by the Parties, confirming compliance or non-compliance of each item of Site Equipment and of the Premises with the applicable Mexican Official Standards, including NOM-081-SEMARNAT-1994 and NOM-085-SEMARNAT-2011. The Delivery Condition Report (including the delivery and acceptance certificate) and Exhibit K shall together constitute the “Baseline Condition Report”.

 

  (d)

Any condition identified in the Delivery Condition Report as non-compliant, deficient or pending shall be corrected by Landlord at its sole cost and expense within [•] days following the Commencement Date, or within such longer period as the Parties agree in writing where correction cannot reasonably be completed within that period, and Landlord’s failure to do so shall entitle Tenant to the remedies set forth in Sections 9(d) and 25. The foregoing applies to any item of Site Equipment or condition of the Premises recorded in Exhibit K as failing to meet an applicable Mexican Official Standard, which Landlord shall remediate, modify, relocate, replace or remove, at its sole cost and expense, within the period set forth in this Section 1(d), without prejudice to Section 3(f). Any condition, defect or non-compliance with Legal Requirements (including urban development, environmental, civil protection, structural, permitting and licensing matters) existing at the Premises or the Site prior to the Commencement Date shall not be the responsibility of either Party, shall be recorded in the Baseline Condition Report and, where its correction is necessary under Legal Requirements or is required by any Governmental Authority, shall be corrected by Landlord at its sole cost and expense within [•] days following notice from either Party (or such longer period as is reasonably necessary, provided Landlord commences the correction within that period and diligently pursues it to completion). Tenant shall be responsible for, and shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Landlord from and against any and all Losses arising out of, any non-compliance or damage caused by the operations of Tenant or its employees, contractors or invitees at the Premises or in the Shared Areas from and after the Commencement Date, and shall correct it at its sole cost and expense within [•] days following notice from Landlord (or such longer period as is reasonably necessary, provided Tenant commences the correction within that period and diligently pursues it to completion), failing which Landlord may exercise the rights set forth in Section 10. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Lease, indemnification in respect of matters covered by this Section 1(d) shall be limited to actual and documented damages finally awarded by a court or arbitral tribunal of competent jurisdiction, or fines and penalties finally imposed by a Governmental Authority.

3. USE; OPERATIONS

 

  (a)

The Premises may be used for the manufacture, assembly, testing, repair, refurbishment and reverse logistics of electronic, electromechanical, medical, automotive and industrial products and components; for receiving, storing, packing, shipping and distributing products, materials, components and merchandise; for warehousing and distribution; for general office, engineering, laboratory, training, cafeteria, medical service, data center and administrative use; for the parking, storage, loading, unloading and circulation of automobiles, trucks and trailers, including driving into and through the Buildings for loading and unloading; for the outdoor storage of Tenant’s Property (being the property described in Section 11(b)); for the installation and operation of rooftop and yard equipment, including solar panels, antennas, emergency generators, compressed air and nitrogen systems, chillers, tanks, batteries and alternative fuel cells; and for any other lawful ancillary or related use (collectively, the “Permitted Uses”). Tenant may use the Premises twenty-four (24) hours a day, seven (7) days a week, fifty-two (52) weeks a year.

 

  (b)

So long as Tenant is FTM, FPL or any Flex Affiliate, the Premises may also be used for any other lawful use that does not increase the demand for services under the SSA beyond the levels committed thereunder and does not require a change in land use or in any Permit held by Landlord.

 

  (c)

Landlord shall not conduct, nor permit any other occupant of the Site to conduct, any activity at the Site that (i) unreasonably interferes with Tenant’s operations, access, logistics or the circulation of trailers described on Exhibit C, (ii) causes vibration, noise, dust, odor, electromagnetic interference or emissions that adversely affect Tenant’s manufacturing processes or the certification of its production lines, or (iii) would cause the cancellation of, or a material increase in the premium of, any insurance policy required to be maintained hereunder. Tenant shall not conduct, nor permit any of the Tenant Parties to conduct, any activity at the Site that (i) unreasonably interferes with

 

A-7

  the operations, access or logistics of Landlord or of the other occupants of the Site, (ii) causes vibration, noise, dust, odor, electromagnetic interference or emissions that adversely affect the operations of Landlord or of the other occupants of the Site, or (iii) would cause the cancellation of, or a material increase in the premium of, any insurance policy required to be maintained hereunder.

 

  (d)

Tenant shall use the Premises in compliance with all Legal Requirements and shall obtain and maintain, at its cost, all Permits relating to its own operations at the Premises, shall comply in full with all conditions and requirements imposed by any Governmental Authority in respect thereof, and shall ensure that its use of the Premises does not cause emissions (in particular noise, odor or light) exceeding the level customary at the location and in the industry, to the extent such use goes beyond the use existing as of the Commencement Date. Landlord shall, at no out-of-pocket cost to Landlord, cooperate with Tenant in obtaining, maintaining, renewing and amending any such Permit, including by executing any application, consent, plan, letter of ownership or authorization required from the owner of the Premises, within [•] Business Days following Tenant’s request. Landlord shall, in turn, obtain and maintain, at its cost, all Permits relating to the Site, the Buildings, the Shared Areas, the Site Equipment and its own operations, and shall comply in full with all conditions and requirements imposed by any Governmental Authority in respect thereof, and Tenant shall, at no out-of-pocket cost to Tenant, cooperate with Landlord in obtaining, maintaining, renewing and amending any such Permit, including by executing any application, consent or authorization required from the occupant of the Premises, within [•] Business Days following Landlord’s request.

 

  (e)

Site Equipment. The Parties acknowledge that certain equipment owned by Landlord, including, without limitation, HVAC systems, chillers and associated building equipment, as well as air conditioning, ventilation, extraction, compressed air and combustion equipment, is installed on, within, above or adjacent to the Buildings comprising the Premises, serves Tenant’s operations in whole or in part, and may be operated by Tenant (the “Site Equipment”). The Site Equipment includes all such equipment existing at the Buildings as of the Commencement Date, and excludes any equipment installed by Tenant, which is governed by Section 11(b). Any item of Site Equipment that exclusively serves one or more of the Buildings comprising the Premises, as identified in the inventory included in Exhibit K, is referred to herein as “Dedicated Site Equipment”. The Site Equipment forms part of the Premises leased hereunder and is not a service provided under the SSA or any Service Level Agreement. The Parties further acknowledge that the Site Equipment is delivered, and Tenant accepts it, in the condition, location and configuration recorded in Exhibit K, including any item recorded there as installed on a temporary basis or as failing to meet an applicable Mexican Official Standard, provided that Tenant shall be responsible for any such failure to the extent caused by the use or operations of the Tenant Parties, as provided in Section 3(f).

 

  (f)

Compliance; Remediation; No Default. Landlord shall at all times keep the Site Equipment in compliance with all Legal Requirements, including the applicable Mexican Official Standards on noise and atmospheric emissions, irrespective of its location and of who operates it, except to the extent that any non-compliance results from Tenant’s failure to perform its maintenance and repair obligations in respect of

 

A-8

  the Dedicated Site Equipment under Section 10, or from the operation of any Site Equipment by the Tenant Parties in breach of the manufacturer’s specifications, in which case Tenant shall be responsible, at its sole cost and expense, for the repair, remediation or other works required to restore such Site Equipment to compliance (and, where any replacement is required as a result, for its cost, as provided in Section 9(c)). Subject to the foregoing, if any item of Site Equipment fails or ceases to meet any such standard, Landlord shall, at Landlord’s election and at Landlord’s sole cost and expense, either (i) remediate, modify, encapsulate, relocate, replace or remove it, and implement any mitigation measure required, within thirty (30) days following notice from Tenant (or, if it cannot reasonably be completed within that period, such longer period as is reasonably necessary, provided Landlord commences it within that period and diligently pursues it to completion), or such shorter period as any Governmental Authority may require, or (ii) indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Tenant Parties from and against any and all Losses arising out of or in connection with that item, including any fine, penalty, surcharge, closure order (clausura), suspension, revocation or conditioning of any Permit, any claim of a neighbor, neighborhood association or third party, any remediation or mitigation cost, and any cost of adapting, relocating or interrupting Tenant’s operations. Landlord may not elect clause (ii) where the non-compliance has resulted, or is reasonably likely to result, in a closure order (clausura), suspension or other measure of a Governmental Authority affecting Tenant’s operations. The operation or use by Tenant of any item of Site Equipment in the condition, location and configuration recorded in Exhibit K shall not constitute a breach of this Lease or an Event of Default by Tenant, nor shall it be asserted by Landlord as a ground for any claim against Tenant, even where that item fails to meet an applicable standard, and no liability of any kind arising out of that condition shall be attributable to Tenant, without prejudice to Tenant’s responsibility for any non-compliance resulting from its failure to maintain and repair the Dedicated Site Equipment as required by Section 10. If Landlord fails to comply with clause (i) within the applicable period, Tenant may exercise the self-help right set forth in Section 9(d), and if any Governmental Authority orders the closure or suspension of all or part of the Premises, or revokes, suspends or conditions any Permit, as a result of the Site Equipment or of any noise, emission, vibration or odor not generated by Tenant’s own equipment, the consequences set forth in Section 16(e) shall apply.

Tenant Equipment and Operations. Tenant shall at all times keep the machinery, equipment, production lines and other installations owned or installed by Tenant, its Affiliates or its customers at the Premises (including any equipment referred to in Section 11(b)), and its use of and operations at the Premises or in the Shared Areas, in compliance with all Legal Requirements, including the applicable Mexican Official Standards on noise and atmospheric emissions, and with the conditions of the Permits relating to its own operations, except to the extent that any non-compliance results from the Site Equipment, from the failure of Landlord to perform its obligations hereunder, or from any act or omission of Landlord or of any other occupant of the Site. If any such equipment, use or operation fails or ceases to meet any such standard, Tenant shall, at Tenant’s election and at its sole cost and expense, either (i) remediate, modify, encapsulate, relocate, replace or remove it, and implement any mitigation measure required, within thirty (30) days following notice from Landlord (or, if it cannot reasonably be completed within that period, such longer period as is

 

A-9

  reasonably necessary, provided Tenant commences it within that period and diligently pursues it to completion), or such shorter period as any Governmental Authority may require, or (ii) indemnify, defend and hold harmless Landlord and its Affiliates from and against any and all Losses arising out of or in connection with that equipment, use or operation, including any fine, penalty, surcharge, closure order (clausura), suspension, revocation or conditioning of any Permit held by Landlord, and any claim of a neighbor, neighborhood association or third party. Tenant may not elect clause (ii) where the non-compliance has resulted, or is reasonably likely to result, in a closure order (clausura), suspension or other measure of a Governmental Authority affecting the Site, Landlord’s operations or any Permit held by Landlord. If Tenant fails to comply with clause (i) within the applicable period, Landlord may exercise the rights set forth in Section 10. Any noise, emission, vibration or odor generated by Tenant’s own equipment or operations shall be for Tenant’s account, and shall not be asserted by Tenant as a ground for any claim against Landlord, rent abatement or termination under this Lease.

 

  (g)

New Equipment. Landlord shall not install or relocate any equipment on, within or above the Buildings comprising the Premises or within the Exclusive Areas, nor install, relocate or modify the operation of any equipment, including any Site Equipment, adjacent thereto where doing so would materially and adversely affect Tenant’s operations or its compliance with any Legal Requirement or Permit, in each case without Tenant’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Tenant shall not install or relocate any equipment in the Shared Areas or elsewhere at the Site outside the Premises, other than as permitted under Sections 3(a) and 8(f), nor install, relocate or modify the operation of any equipment where doing so would materially and adversely affect the structure of the Buildings, the Site infrastructure, the operations of Landlord or of the other occupants of the Site, or Landlord’s compliance with any Legal Requirement or Permit, in each case without Landlord’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

 

  (h)

Complaints, Monitoring and Attribution. Each Party shall notify the other, within [•] Business Days, of any complaint, claim, letter, requirement, inspection, proceeding or order received from a neighbor, a neighborhood association or any Governmental Authority in respect of noise, atmospheric emissions, vibration or odor at the Site. Landlord shall, at its cost, (i) cause perimeter measurements of noise and emissions to be taken at least once every [•] months by a laboratory or verification unit accredited before the Mexican Accreditation Entity, at the points recorded in Exhibit K, and deliver the results to Tenant, and (ii) maintain the mitigation plan and the periodic meetings with the neighboring developments, in which Tenant shall be entitled to participate, and implement at its cost any mitigation measure relating to the Site, the Shared Areas or the Site Equipment, except to the extent caused by the Tenant Parties’ operations or use, in which case Tenant shall bear the costs attributable thereto. Tenant shall deliver to Landlord the results of any measurement of noise or emissions taken by or for Tenant in respect of its operations at the Premises, shall cooperate in good faith with Landlord in the mitigation plan and the periodic meetings referred to in clause (ii), and shall implement at its cost any mitigation measure relating to its own equipment or operations, as provided in Section 3(f).

4. TERM; EXTENSION; YEAR-25 ELECTION

 

  (a)

Primary Term. The Lease Term shall commence on the Commencement Date and, unless earlier terminated in accordance herewith, shall continue for twenty-five (25) years (the “Primary Term”).

 

  (b)

Landlord Bound for the Full Term. The Primary Term is mandatory and irrevocable for Landlord for its entire duration. Landlord shall have no right to terminate this Lease, to refuse extension in accordance with Addendum 2, or to cease performance hereunder, prior to the expiration of the Primary Term, except pursuant to Section 26(c) following an Event of Default by Tenant that remains uncured after the expiration of the applicable cure period set forth in Section 26(a). Tenant’s termination rights are as set forth in Section 24. Nothing in this Lease shall exclude or limit the right of either Party to terminate this Lease for serious cause where such right cannot be waived under applicable law.

 

  (c)

Statutory Extension. Nothing in this Lease shall be construed as a waiver by Tenant of its right, under Article 2051 of the Civil Code of the State of Jalisco, to an extension of the Lease Term equal to one fourth (1/4) of the period agreed herein, computed from the date on which Tenant took possession of the Premises as tenant, which right the Parties expressly acknowledge and preserve. Any extension exercised under Addendum 2 shall be in addition to, and not in substitution of, that statutory right, and Tenant may elect to exercise either or both.

 

  (d)

Year-25 Election. No later than twelve (12) months prior to the expiration of the Primary Term, Tenant may deliver written notice to Landlord electing, at Tenant’s sole discretion, either or both of the following, and Landlord shall be obligated to implement the election so made:

 

  (i)

Extension. An extension of the occupancy of the Premises on the same terms and conditions as those set forth in this Lease, except that the Base Rent for the first year of each extension period shall be the Market Rent determined in accordance with Section 4(f), and shall thereafter be adjusted annually in accordance with Section 5(c), for an additional one (1) period of [•] years. Given the limit established by Article 2045 of the Civil Code of the State of Jalisco, the Parties agree that Landlord’s obligation under this paragraph constitutes an irrevocable offer to enter into a new lease agreement in respect of the Premises, on the same terms and conditions as this Lease, save for the Base Rent determined as aforesaid, for the period elected by Tenant, which offer Landlord may not withdraw and which Tenant may accept by delivering the notice contemplated in this Section 4(d), whereupon the Parties shall execute such new lease agreement within [•] days following the determination of the Market Rent.

 

  (ii)

Usufruct. The constitution in Tenant’s favor of a usufruct over the Premises, for the maximum period permitted by applicable law and on the same terms and conditions, mutatis mutandis as those set forth in this Lease, with the consideration for the usufruct determined on the basis of the Market Rent, as provided in Addendum 4.

 

  (e)

If Tenant delivers no notice under Section 4(d) and the Lease Term expires, Tenant shall surrender the Premises in accordance with Section 26(e), without prejudice to Tenant’s statutory rights under Section 4(c), during which Tenant’s rights under Section 23 shall continue to apply.

 

A-11

  (f)

Market Rent. For purposes of Section 4(d), “Market Rent” means the monthly rent per square foot that a willing tenant would pay and a willing landlord would accept, at arm’s length, for the lease of premises comparable to the Premises in the Guadalajara metropolitan area, for a term equal to the applicable extension period, taking into account the terms and conditions of this Lease (including its gross lease structure and the allocation of maintenance, repair and replacement obligations hereunder), and disregarding the value of any alteration, improvement or equipment made or installed by Tenant at its cost. The Market Rent shall be determined by an independent valuer selected from among Colliers, CBRE, JLL and Cushman & Wakefield (or their respective Mexican affiliates), [jointly appointed by the Parties within [•] days following delivery of Tenant’s notice under Section 4(d) or, failing agreement within that period, designated by lot (sorteo) from among those firms, before a notary public, at the request of either Party], provided that the valuer shall not have provided services to either Party or its Affiliates in respect of the Site during the [•] months preceding its appointment. The valuer shall deliver its determination to both Parties within [•] days following its appointment, and such determination shall be final and binding on the Parties, absent manifest error. The fees of the valuer shall be borne by the Parties in equal shares. Tenant may withdraw its election under Section 4(d)(i) by written notice to Landlord delivered within [•] days following receipt of the valuer’s determination, without liability, other than the reimbursement to Landlord of the portion of the fees of the valuer borne by Landlord, in which case this Lease shall expire at the end of the Lease Term then in effect, without prejudice to Tenant’s rights under Section 4(c).

No such cost shall be charged or passed through to Tenant, whether as additional rent, as a common area or maintenance charge, under the SSA or any Service Level Agreement, or in any other form, except as expressly provided in this Section 9, in Section 10 and in Section 7(b)(i). For purposes of this Lease, the “replacement” of any item of Site Equipment means its substitution, or the substitution of any of its major components, when it has reached the end of its useful life or can no longer be repaired on a commercially reasonable basis, as reasonably determined by the manufacturer or a qualified independent technician; provided that, to the extent any such replacement is required as a result of an act or omission of the Tenant Parties (including Tenant’s failure to perform its maintenance and repair obligations under Section 10), its cost shall be borne by Tenant. Notwithstanding the foregoing, to the extent any maintenance, repair, replacement or other works, including works required by a Governmental Authority, are required as a result of the acts, omissions, operations or use of the Premises or Shared Areas by the Tenant Parties, their cost shall be borne by Tenant, subject to Sections 9(a) and 9(e).

Tenant shall not be responsible for (i) any repair or replacement arising out of a structural defect, a latent defect, a construction defect or the failure of Landlord to perform its obligations hereunder, (ii) the replacement of any Site Equipment, including the Dedicated Site Equipment, except as provided in Sections 9(a) and 9(c), the maintenance or repair of any Site Equipment other than the Dedicated Site Equipment, or any capital replacement of Building systems or equipment, except as provided in Section 9, or (iii) any repair arising out of the act or omission of Landlord or of any other occupant of the Site; provided that, notwithstanding the foregoing, Tenant shall bear the cost of any repair or replacement to the extent required as a result of damage caused by the Tenant Parties, including damage to the roof, roof membrane or structure caused by Tenant’s rooftop equipment, signage or alterations, as provided in Section 9(a). Tenant shall also, at its cost, maintain and repair non-structural exterior areas within its Exclusive Areas and be responsible for the costs of cleaning, maintaining and repairing the Shared Areas to the extent required as a result of the Tenant Parties’ operations or use, including damage caused thereby; provided that Landlord shall perform work affecting structural elements, roofs or Site infrastructure (and Tenant shall bear the cost to the extent attributable to the Tenant Parties).

Where any delimitation, separation or metering is required as a result of a request of Tenant, its cost shall be borne by the Parties in equal shares, except where required as a result of a partial termination by Tenant under Section 24(a), in which case its cost shall be borne solely by Tenant.

Tenant shall use the Shared Areas with care and on a non-exclusive basis, during the operating hours and in accordance with the site rules applicable to all users as notified by Landlord from time to time, shall not store any property or obstruct any Shared Area, and shall be liable for any damage to the Shared Areas caused by the Tenant Parties. A temporary restriction or unavailability of any Shared Area that does not materially impair Tenant’s operations shall not entitle Tenant to any reduction of Rent.

Landlord shall have no unilateral right of relocation, and no provision of this Lease or of the SSA shall be construed as granting such a right.

Tenant shall have [•] days following receipt of the ROFO Notice to elect to purchase the Offered Property on the terms set forth therein, in which case the Parties shall execute a purchase agreement substantially in the form attached as Exhibit E and shall close on the closing date set forth in the ROFO Notice or the ROFR Notice, as applicable, or, if later, within [•] days thereafter. Tenant’s election, once given, shall be irrevocable. Landlord’s offer contained in the ROFO Notice or the ROFR Notice shall likewise be irrevocable during the applicable exercise period. Tenant shall bear any transfer tax, registration fees, notarial costs and other costs of the acquisition, and shall obtain at its own risk and cost any approval required for the acquisition. Landlord shall bear any income tax payable on the disposition, the costs of cancelling any lien or encumbrance and of delivering title to the Offered Property in accordance with Exhibit E, and the fees of its own advisors. Tenant’s rights under this Section 23 shall not be exercisable while an Event of Default by Tenant is continuing, and shall lapse if Tenant fails to close in accordance with this Section 23(b) for reasons not attributable to Landlord.

If Tenant does not exercise its right of first offer, and Landlord thereafter receives an offer from a third party, or proposes to sell the Offered Property, on a price, form of payment or closing date more favorable to the purchaser than those set forth in the ROFO Notice, including any reduction in price of more than [•] percent ([•]%), Landlord shall deliver written notice to Tenant specifying only such price, form of payment and closing date (the “ROFR Notice”), without any obligation to disclose the identity of the third party or any other term of its offer, and Tenant shall have [•] days following receipt to elect to purchase the Offered Property on such price, form of payment and closing date, in which case the Parties shall proceed as set forth in Section 23(b).

Continuing Rights. Tenant’s rights under this Section 23 are continuing rights, exercisable on each and every occasion on which Landlord proposes a disposition during the Lease Term and any extension thereof, and shall not be extinguished by any failure to exercise them on a prior occasion. If Tenant does not exercise its rights in respect of a proposed disposition, Landlord may complete it with a third party, on a price, form of payment and closing date no more favorable to the purchaser than those last offered to Tenant, within [•] months following the expiration of Tenant’s last exercise period; if the disposition is not completed within that period, Tenant’s rights shall apply again to any subsequent proposed disposition. Any disposition made in violation of this Section 23 shall be null and void and shall not be enforceable against Tenant, which nullity shall be Tenant’s sole remedy in respect of such violation.

29. FORCE MAJEURE

 

  (a)

Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure in the performance of its obligations hereunder (other than the payment of money) to the extent caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, including acts of God, natural disaster, epidemic, pandemic, fire, flood, earthquake, war, civil disorder, act of a Governmental Authority not attributable to the affected Party, strike or labor disturbance not involving such Party’s own workforce, and failure of a supplier of electricity or water not within such Party’s reasonable control (each, a “Force Majeure” event), provided that the affected Party notifies the other promptly and uses commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate and to resume performance.

 

  (b)

Base Rent shall abate during any Force Majeure event that prevents Tenant from using or accessing all or a material portion of the Premises for more than thirty (30) consecutive days, from the commencement of such event until use or access is restored, in proportion to the portion affected, and if such event continues for more than [•] consecutive days, either Party may terminate this Lease upon written notice.

 

  (c)

Force Majeure shall not excuse Landlord from its obligations under Section 16, except as provided in Section 16(f), nor from any payment or indemnity obligation unless such indemnity obligation is impacted by a Force Majeure event. Force Majeure shall likewise not excuse Tenant from any payment or indemnity obligation unless such indemnity obligation is impacted by a Force Majeure event, without prejudice to the abatement of Base Rent provided in Section 29(b).

If Landlord fails to comply with clause (i) within the applicable period, Tenant may exercise the self-help right set forth in Section 9(d), and if any Governmental Authority orders the closure or suspension of all or part of the Premises, or revokes, suspends or conditions any Permit, as a result of the Site Equipment or of any noise, emission, vibration or odor not generated by Tenant’s own equipment, the consequences set forth in Section 16(e) shall apply.

Tenant Equipment and Operations. Tenant shall at all times keep the machinery, equipment, production lines and other installations owned or installed by Tenant, its Affiliates or its customers at the Premises (including any equipment referred to in Section 11(b)), and its use of and operations at the Premises or in the Shared Areas, in compliance with all Legal Requirements, including the applicable Mexican Official Standards on noise and atmospheric emissions, and with the conditions of the Permits relating to its own operations, except to the extent that any non-compliance results from the Site Equipment, from the failure of Landlord to perform its obligations hereunder, or from any act or omission of Landlord or of any other occupant of the Site. If any such equipment, use or operation fails or ceases to meet any such standard, Tenant shall, at Tenant’s election and at its sole cost and expense, either (i) remediate, modify, encapsulate, relocate, replace or remove it, and implement any mitigation measure required, within thirty (30) days following notice from Landlord (or, if it cannot reasonably be completed within that period, such longer period as is

reasonably necessary, provided Tenant commences it within that period and diligently pursues it to completion), or such shorter period as any Governmental Authority may require, or (ii) indemnify, defend and hold harmless Landlord and its Affiliates from and against any and all Losses arising out of or in connection with that equipment, use or operation, including any fine, penalty, surcharge, closure order (clausura), suspension, revocation or conditioning of any Permit held by Landlord, and any claim of a neighbor, neighborhood association or third party. Tenant may not elect clause (ii) where the non-compliance has resulted, or is reasonably likely to result, in a closure order (clausura), suspension or other measure of a Governmental Authority affecting the Site, Landlord’s operations or any Permit held by Landlord. Tenant shall not install or relocate any equipment in the Shared Areas or elsewhere at the Site outside the Premises, other than as permitted under Sections 3(a) and 8(f), nor install, relocate or modify the operation of any equipment where doing so would materially and adversely affect the structure of the Buildings, the Site infrastructure, the operations of Landlord or of the other occupants of the Site, or Landlord’s compliance with any Legal Requirement or Permit, in each case without Landlord’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

Landlord shall, at its cost, (i) cause perimeter measurements of noise and emissions to be taken at least once every [•] months by a laboratory or verification unit accredited before the Mexican Accreditation Entity, at the points recorded in Exhibit K, and deliver the results to Tenant, and (ii) maintain the mitigation plan and the periodic meetings with the neighboring developments, in which Tenant shall be entitled to participate, and implement at its cost any mitigation measure relating to the Site, the Shared Areas or the Site Equipment, except to the extent caused by the Tenant Parties’ operations or use, in which case Tenant shall bear the costs attributable thereto. Tenant shall deliver to Landlord the results of any measurement of noise or emissions taken by or for Tenant in respect of its operations at the Premises, shall cooperate in good faith with Landlord in the mitigation plan and the periodic meetings referred to in clause (ii), and shall implement at its cost any mitigation measure relating to its own equipment or operations, as provided in Section 3(f).

4. TERM; EXTENSION; YEAR-25 ELECTION

 

  (a)

Primary Term. The Lease Term shall commence on the Commencement Date and, unless earlier terminated in accordance herewith, shall continue for twenty-five (25) years (the “Primary Term”).

 

  (b)

Landlord Bound for the Full Term. The Primary Term is mandatory and irrevocable for Landlord for its entire duration. Landlord shall have no right to terminate this Lease, to refuse extension in accordance with Addendum 2, or to cease performance hereunder, prior to the expiration of the Primary Term, except pursuant to Section 26(c) following an Event of Default by Tenant that remains uncured after the expiration of the applicable cure period set forth in Section 26(a). Tenant’s termination rights are as set forth in Section 24. Nothing in this Lease shall exclude or limit the right of either Party to terminate this Lease for serious cause where such right cannot be waived under applicable law.

 

  (c)

Statutory Extension. Nothing in this Lease shall be construed as a waiver by Tenant of its right, under Article 2051 of the Civil Code of the State of Jalisco, to an extension of the Lease Term equal to one fourth (1/4) of the period agreed herein, computed from the date on which Tenant took possession of the Premises as tenant, which right the Parties expressly acknowledge and preserve. Any extension exercised under Addendum 2 shall be in addition to, and not in substitution of, that statutory right, and Tenant may elect to exercise either or both.

 

  (d)

Year-25 Election. No later than twelve (12) months prior to the expiration of the Primary Term, Tenant may deliver written notice to Landlord electing, at Tenant’s sole discretion, either or both of the following, and Landlord shall be obligated to implement the election so made:

 

  (i)

Extension. An extension of the occupancy of the Premises on the same terms and conditions as those set forth in this Lease, except that the Base Rent for the first year of each extension period shall be the Market Rent determined in accordance with Section 4(f), and shall thereafter be adjusted annually in accordance with Section 5(c), for an additional one (1) period of [•] years. Given the limit established by Article 2045 of the Civil Code of the State of Jalisco, the Parties agree that Landlord’s obligation under this paragraph constitutes an irrevocable offer to enter into a new lease agreement in respect of the Premises, on the same terms and conditions as this Lease, save for the Base Rent determined as aforesaid, for the period elected by Tenant, which offer Landlord may not withdraw and which Tenant may accept by delivering the notice contemplated in this Section 4(d), whereupon the Parties shall execute such new lease agreement within [•] days following the determination of the Market Rent.

 

  (ii)

Usufruct. The constitution in Tenant’s favor of a usufruct over the Premises, for the maximum period permitted by applicable law and on the same terms and conditions, mutatis mutandis as those set forth in this Lease, with the consideration for the usufruct determined on the basis of the Market Rent, as provided in Addendum 4.

 

  (e)

If Tenant delivers no notice under Section 4(d) and the Lease Term expires, Tenant shall surrender the Premises in accordance with Section 26(e), without prejudice to Tenant’s statutory rights under Section 4(c), during which Tenant’s rights under Section 23 shall continue to apply.

 

A-55

  (f)

Market Rent. For purposes of Section 4(d), “Market Rent” means the monthly rent per square foot that a willing tenant would pay and a willing landlord would accept, at arm’s length, for the lease of premises comparable to the Premises in the Guadalajara metropolitan area, for a term equal to the applicable extension period, taking into account the terms and conditions of this Lease (including its gross lease structure and the allocation of maintenance, repair and replacement obligations hereunder), and disregarding the value of any alteration, improvement or equipment made or installed by Tenant at its cost. The Market Rent shall be determined by an independent valuer selected from among Colliers, CBRE, JLL and Cushman & Wakefield (or their respective Mexican affiliates), [jointly appointed by the Parties within [•] days following delivery of Tenant’s notice under Section 4(d) or, failing agreement within that period, designated by lot (sorteo) from among those firms, before a notary public, at the request of either Party], provided that the valuer shall not have provided services to either Party or its Affiliates in respect of the Site during the [•] months preceding its appointment. The valuer shall deliver its determination to both Parties within [•] days following its appointment, and such determination shall be final and binding on the Parties, absent manifest error. The fees of the valuer shall be borne by the Parties in equal shares. Tenant may withdraw its election under Section 4(d)(i) by written notice to Landlord delivered within [•] days following receipt of the valuer’s determination, without liability, other than the reimbursement to Landlord of the portion of the fees of the valuer borne by Landlord, in which case this Lease shall expire at the end of the Lease Term then in effect, without prejudice to Tenant’s rights under Section 4(c).

  (a)

Tenant shall not be responsible for (i) any repair or replacement arising out of a structural defect, a latent defect, a construction defect or the failure of Landlord to perform its obligations hereunder, (ii) the replacement of any Site Equipment, including the Dedicated Site Equipment, except as provided in Sections 9(a) and 9(c), the maintenance or repair of any Site Equipment other than the Dedicated Site Equipment, or any capital replacement of Building systems or equipment, except as provided in Section 9, or (iii) any repair arising out of the act or omission of Landlord or of any other occupant of the Site; provided that, notwithstanding the foregoing, Tenant shall bear the cost of any repair or replacement to the extent required as a result of damage caused by the Tenant Parties, including damage to the roof, roof membrane or structure caused by Tenant’s rooftop equipment, signage or alterations, as provided in Section 9(a). Tenant shall also, at its cost, maintain and repair non-structural exterior areas within its Exclusive Areas and be responsible for the costs of cleaning, maintaining and repairing the Shared Areas to the extent required as a result of the Tenant Parties’ operations or use, including damage caused thereby; provided that Landlord shall perform work affecting structural elements, roofs or Site infrastructure (and Tenant shall bear the cost to the extent attributable to the Tenant Parties).

  (a)

23. RIGHT OF FIRST OFFER; RIGHT OF FIRST REFUSAL

 

  (a)

Scope. Tenant’s rights under this Section 23 apply to any sale, transfer or other disposition by Landlord of the Premises, or of any Parcel, portion of the Site or the Site as a whole that includes all or any portion of the Premises (each, an “Offered Property”). Tenant’s rights shall be exercisable only in respect of the Offered Property as a whole, on the terms offered by Landlord, and Landlord shall have no obligation to subdivide, individualize or otherwise separate the Premises or any portion thereof for that purpose.

 

  (b)

Right of First Offer. If Landlord intends to sell, transfer or otherwise dispose of any Offered Property, Landlord shall first deliver written notice to Tenant specifying the Offered Property and only the price, the form of payment and the proposed closing date on which Landlord is willing to sell (the “ROFO Notice”), the remaining terms of the acquisition being those set forth in Exhibit E. Tenant shall have [•] days following receipt of the ROFO Notice to elect to purchase the Offered Property on the terms set forth therein, in which case the Parties shall execute a purchase agreement substantially in the form attached as Exhibit E and shall close on the closing date set forth in the ROFO Notice or the ROFR Notice, as applicable, or, if later, within [•] days thereafter. Tenant’s election, once given, shall be irrevocable. Landlord’s offer contained in the ROFO Notice or the ROFR Notice shall likewise be irrevocable during the applicable exercise period. Tenant shall bear any transfer tax, registration fees, notarial costs and other costs of the acquisition, and shall obtain at its own risk and cost any approval required for the acquisition. Landlord shall bear any income tax payable on the disposition, the costs of cancelling any lien or encumbrance and of delivering title to the Offered Property in accordance with Exhibit E, and the fees of its own advisors. Tenant’s rights under this Section 23 shall not be exercisable while an Event of Default by Tenant is continuing, and shall lapse if Tenant fails to close in accordance with this Section 23(b) for reasons not attributable to Landlord.

 

  (c)

Right of First Refusal. If Tenant does not exercise its right of first offer, and Landlord thereafter receives an offer from a third party, or proposes to sell the Offered Property, on a price, form of payment or closing date more favorable to the purchaser than those set forth in the ROFO Notice, including any reduction in price of more than [•] percent ([•]%), Landlord shall deliver written notice to Tenant specifying only such price, form of payment and closing date (the “ROFR Notice”), without any obligation to disclose the identity of the third party or any other term of its offer, and Tenant shall have [•] days following receipt to elect to purchase the Offered Property on such price, form of payment and closing date, in which case the Parties shall proceed as set forth in Section 23(b).

 

  (d)

Continuing Rights. Tenant’s rights under this Section 23 are continuing rights, exercisable on each and every occasion on which Landlord proposes a disposition during the Lease Term and any extension thereof, and shall not be extinguished by any failure to exercise them on a prior occasion. If Tenant does not exercise its rights in respect of a proposed disposition, Landlord may complete it with a third party, on a price, form of payment and closing date no more favorable to the purchaser than those last offered to Tenant, within [•] months following the expiration of Tenant’s last exercise period; if the disposition is not completed within that period, Tenant’s rights shall apply again to any subsequent proposed disposition. Any disposition made in violation of this Section 23 shall be null and void and shall not be enforceable against Tenant, which nullity shall be Tenant’s sole remedy in respect of such violation.

29. FORCE MAJEURE

 

  (a)

Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure in the performance of its obligations hereunder (other than the payment of money) to the extent caused by an event beyond its reasonable control, including acts of God, natural disaster, epidemic, pandemic, fire, flood, earthquake, war, civil disorder, act of a Governmental Authority not attributable to the affected Party, strike or labor disturbance not involving such Party’s own workforce, and failure of a supplier of electricity or water not within such Party’s reasonable control (each, a “Force Majeure” event), provided that the affected Party notifies the other promptly and uses commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate and to resume performance.

 

  (b)

Base Rent shall abate during any Force Majeure event that prevents Tenant from using or accessing all or a material portion of the Premises for more than thirty (30) consecutive days, from the commencement of such event until use or access is restored, in proportion to the portion affected, and if such event continues for more than [•] consecutive days, either Party may terminate this Lease upon written notice.

 

  (c)

Force Majeure shall not excuse Landlord from its obligations under Section 16, except as provided in Section 16(f), nor from any payment or indemnity obligation unless such indemnity obligation is impacted by a Force Majeure event. Force Majeure shall likewise not excuse Tenant from any payment or indemnity obligation unless such indemnity obligation is impacted by a Force Majeure event, without prejudice to the abatement of Base Rent provided in Section 29(b).

Wherever this Lease provides that the consent of a Party shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed, the requesting Party shall deliver a written request together with information reasonably sufficient to evaluate it, and the other Party shall respond within [•] Business Days following its receipt of such request and information; provided that the responding Party may, within [•] Business Days following such receipt, request in writing such additional information as it reasonably requires, in which case such [•] Business Day period shall run from its receipt of such additional information. Any refusal shall state the reasons therefor in reasonable detail. If the responding Party fails to respond within the applicable period, the requesting Party may deliver a second written notice expressly referring to this Section 36(j) and stating in bold capital letters: “FAILURE TO RESPOND WITHIN [•] BUSINESS DAYS SHALL RESULT IN THE REQUESTED CONSENT BEING DEEMED GRANTED,” and if no response is received within [•] Business Days following receipt of that second notice, the consent shall be deemed granted. This Section 36(j) shall not apply to any consent required under Sections 1(b), 3(g), 11(a), 15(c) or 20, or to any matter affecting the structure of the Buildings, title to any Parcel, or any Permit held by the other Party, each of which must be express.

 

  (k)

Definitions. For purposes of this Lease, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below, and the other capitalized terms used herein shall have the meanings given to them elsewhere in this Lease:

“Affiliate” means, with respect to any person, any other person that directly or indirectly, through one or more intermediaries, controls, is controlled by or is under common control with such person, where “control” means the power to direct the management and policies of a person, whether through the ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of its voting shares or equity interests, by contract or otherwise; provided that, for purposes of this Lease, Landlord shall not be deemed an Affiliate of Tenant, nor Tenant an Affiliate of Landlord.

SITE SERVICES AGREEMENT (GUAD NORTH)

This SITE SERVICES AGREEMENT (GUAD NORTH) is entered into as of [•] (the “Signing Date”), by and between PARQUE DE TECNOLOGÍA ELECTRÓNICA, S.A. DE C.V., a Mexican entity existing under the laws of Mexico (“Provider”), and FLEXTRONICS PLASTICS, S.A. DE C.V., a Mexican entity existing under the laws of Mexico (“Recipient”). Provider and Recipient are at times referred to herein individually as a “Party” and collectively as the “Parties.” This Agreement shall become effective with respect to a Service on the date set forth on the applicable SLA (each, an “Effective Date”).

W I T N E S S E T H:

WHEREAS, Flex Ltd. and Archer SpinCo, Inc. are parties to that certain Separation and Distribution Agreement, dated as of [•] (as amended from time to time, the “Separation Agreement”), pursuant to which their respective businesses and operations are being separated; and

WHEREAS, in connection with the transactions contemplated by the Separation Agreement, Provider has agreed to provide certain Services (as hereinafter defined) to Recipient at the Site (as hereinafter defined) pursuant to this Agreement.

NOW, THEREFORE, subject to the terms, conditions, covenants and provisions of this Agreement, for good and valuable consideration, the sufficiency and receipt of which are hereby acknowledged, and intending to be legally bound, Provider and Recipient mutually covenant and agree as follows:

ARTICLE I

DEFINITIONS

Section 1.01 Definitions. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed thereto in the Separation Agreement. As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the following meanings:

“Action” shall mean any demand, action, claim, cause of action, suit, countersuit, arbitration, inquiry, case, litigation, subpoena, proceeding or investigation (whether civil, criminal or administrative and whether at law or in equity) by or before any court or grand jury, any Governmental Entity or any arbitration or mediation tribunal or authority.

“Affiliate” has the meaning set forth in the Separation Agreement.

“Agreement” shall mean this Site Services Agreement (Guad North) and includes all Schedules and SLAs hereto, as amended, modified or supplemented from time to time in accordance with its terms.

 

B-1

“Applicable Exchange Rate” shall mean the Bloomberg fixing rate at 5:00 p.m. New York City Time on the date that is two Business Days before the date the payment is required to be made or, as applicable, on which an invoice is submitted (provided, however, that with regard to any payments in respect of Losses for payments made to Third Parties, the date shall be the Business Day before the relevant payment was made to the Third Party) or in the Wall Street Journal on such date if not so published on Bloomberg.

“Business Day” has the meaning set forth in the Separation Agreement.

“Calendar Year” shall mean a period of twelve (12) consecutive calendar months commencing on any January 1.

“Change” shall mean each change to the nature or the manner of performing a Service, including (a) a material decrease (including in duration) in the service level applicable to any Service, (b) any additional service, or (c) any change to the Specifications for the provision of such Service.

“Change Request” shall mean a written description of a proposed Change.

“Claim” or “Claims” shall mean any claim, whether actual or potential, known or unknown, suspected or unsuspected, contingent or non-contingent, whether concealed or hidden, upon any theory of law or equity, based upon past or future events, now existing or coming into existence in the future.

“Code” shall mean the U.S. Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended.

“Consent Costs” shall mean all out-of-pocket costs paid or coming due before or after the Effective Date with respect to the Site associated with securing consents from Third Parties that are required to provide the Services to Recipient at the Site.

“Contamination” means the Release of any Hazardous Material to, on, onto or into the environment.

“Contract” shall mean any written contract, lease, license, agreement, instrument or other commitment that is binding on any Person or entity or any part of its property under applicable Law, other than a Permit.

“Contract Manager” shall have the meaning set forth in Section 10.01.

“Critical Service” shall mean any Service expressly designated as a “Critical Service” in the applicable SLA.

“Default Rate” shall mean, for any day, a rate per annum equal to the lesser of (i) the Prime Rate then in effect plus two percent (2%) and (ii) the maximum rate of interest permitted by applicable Law.

“Defaulting Party” shall have the meaning set forth in Section 6.02(a).

“Dispute” has the meaning set forth in the Separation Agreement.

 

B-2

“Due Date” shall have the meaning set forth in Section 3.03(a).

“Effective Date” shall have the meaning set forth in the Preamble.

“EH&S Policies” shall mean the bona fide environmental, health and safety policies and procedures in effect at the Site from time to time, in each case to the extent applicable to the relevant access or activities and communicated to the applicable Party in advance.

“Environmental Laws” shall mean, collectively, any and all Laws, Judgments or other legal requirements of a Governmental Entity relating to Contamination, pollution, human health or safety, or protection of the environment, air, soil, subsoil, surface water, groundwater or natural or biotic resources, including Laws relating to the exposure to, or Release, threatened Release (including investigation and clean-up of such Release) or the presence of Hazardous Materials, or otherwise relating to the manufacture, processing, distribution, import, registration, notification, labeling, use, treatment, storage, transport, disposal or handling of Hazardous Materials and all Laws with regard to recordkeeping, notification, disclosure and reporting requirements respecting Hazardous Materials.

“Environmental Permits” shall have the meaning set forth in Section 9.02(a).

“Essential Site Service” shall mean any Service identified in the applicable SLA as necessary for continuous access to, occupancy of or lawful operation of Recipient’s Facility. The designation of a Service as an Essential Site Service shall not, by itself, cause such Service to be a Critical Service for purposes of Article VIII.

“Facility” shall mean the Provider’s Facility and/or the Recipient’s Facility, as applicable.

“Force Majeure” shall mean, for each Party, any circumstance(s) beyond the reasonable control of that Party which has the effect of materially delaying, hindering or preventing, in whole or in part, the performance of such Party’s obligations under this Agreement, including, but not limited to, any of the following events:

(a) acts of God or acts of providence that result in a shutdown, failure, incapacity or reduced capacity of the facilities associated with the performance of this Agreement, including epidemics, landslides, hurricanes, floods, washouts, fires, lightning, earthquakes, storm warnings, perils of the sea, extreme heat or extreme cold, and other adverse weather conditions and threats of any of the foregoing, and whether preceded by, concurrent with, or followed by acts or omissions of any human agency (other than the affected Party’s employees or contractors, or the affected Party’s vendors or suppliers who are under the reasonable control of the affected Party), whether foreseeable or not;

(b) acts or omissions of Governmental Entities not resulting from any breach of this Agreement or failure to comply with applicable Law or Permits by the Party claiming to be affected by such event (or its Affiliates);

(c) acts of civil disorder including acts of sabotage, acts of the public enemy, acts of war (declared or undeclared), blockades, insurrections, riots, mass protests or demonstrations or threats of any of the foregoing, and police action in connection with or in reaction to any such act of civil disorder;

 

B-3

(d) acts of industrial disorder, including strikes, lockouts, picketing and threats of any of the foregoing, when any such act of industrial disorder directly or indirectly results in the inability of the affected Party to perform its obligations under this Agreement, regardless of whether the settlement of any labor dispute to prevent or end any such act of industrial disorder is within the sole discretion of the Party involved in such labor dispute;

(e) failure of any suppliers to supply materials to the affected Party, including the failure of any electric energy provider, such as a public electric utility, to supply electric energy to the affected Party, except to the extent resulting from the affected Party’s breach or default under, or failure to pay amounts due pursuant to, the applicable agreement with such Third Party; and

(f) failures of equipment, except to the extent resulting from the affected Party’s failure to maintain, repair or operate such equipment in accordance with this Agreement or the applicable SLA;

provided that, in each case, such event materially impacts the assets or operations required for the applicable Party’s performance under this Agreement and is not under or within the reasonable control of the Party (or its Affiliates) claiming to be affected by such event; provided, further, that no Force Majeure shall be deemed to exist to the extent the applicable event results from such Party’s breach of this Agreement or failure to comply with applicable Law or Permits.

Force Majeure shall not include (i) lack of funds, (ii) any voluntary sale, transfer or encumbrance by the affected Party, to the extent such action causes the claimed inability to perform, or (iii) the affected Party’s failure to maintain or timely renew any Permit, license, access right or other right within such Party’s reasonable control and required for its performance under this Agreement.

“Governmental Entity” shall mean any national, state, municipal, local, supranational or foreign government or any court or other tribunal of competent jurisdiction, regulatory or administrative authority, arbitral body (public or private), agency or commission or other national, state, local, supranational or foreign governmental authority or instrumentality (excluding any state-owned enterprise or similar entity).

“Guadalajara Lease” shall mean that certain lease, dated as of [•], by and between Parque de Tecnología Electrónica, S.A. de C.V., as landlord, and FLEXTRONICS PLASTICS, S.A. DE C.V., as tenant, as amended, supplemented or otherwise modified from time to time in accordance with its terms.

“Hazardous Material” shall mean (a) any petroleum or petroleum products, radioactive materials, radon, asbestos or asbestos-containing materials in any form, lead-based paint, urea formaldehyde, foam insulation, per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances or polychlorinated biphenyls; or (b) any chemicals, materials, substances, compounds, mixtures, products or byproducts, biological agents, pollutants, contaminants or wastes (or combination thereof) that are now or hereafter become listed, defined or characterized as or included in the definition of “hazardous substances,” “hazardous wastes,” “hazardous materials,” “extremely hazardous wastes,” “restricted hazardous wastes,” “special waste,” “toxic substances,” “pollutants,” “contaminants,” “toxic,” “dangerous,” “corrosive,” “flammable,” “reactive,” “radioactive,” or words of similar import under any Environmental Law.

“Indemnified Party” shall have the meaning set forth in Section 9.03(a).

“Indemnifying Party” shall have the meaning set forth in Section 9.03(a).

“Intellectual Property” shall have the meaning set forth in the Separation Agreement.

“Intentional Misconduct” means an act or omission of a Person that is (a) in breach of this Agreement; and (b) intended to cause the consequences such act or omission would have on the rights, business, operations, property, health or safety of another Person. “Intentional Misconduct” shall include:

any intentional full or partial shutdown or full or partial slowdown of a Facility by a Party, in each case, in breach of this Agreement and undertaken with such specific intent; and

“Judgment” shall mean any judgment, injunction, ruling, award, order, determination, decree or writ of any Governmental Entity, arbitrator or arbitral tribunal.

“Liability” or “Liabilities” shall mean any and all indebtedness, liabilities, guarantees, assurances, commitments and obligations of any kind or nature, whether fixed, contingent or absolute, asserted or unasserted, matured or unmatured, liquidated or unliquidated, accrued or not accrued, known or unknown, due or to become due, reflected on a balance sheet or otherwise, whenever or however arising, including, but not limited to, those arising under any Law or Judgment, Contract or tort based on negligence or strict liability.

“Losses” shall mean all losses, Liabilities, claims, fines, deficiencies, damages, payments (including those arising out of any settlement or Judgment relating to any Action), interest, obligations, penalties, fees and costs and expenses of any kind (including reasonable accountants’ and attorneys’ fees and disbursements incurred in the defense thereof).

“Maintenance Expenditure” shall mean any expenditure including capital expenditures for renewal, replacement, rehabilitation, unplanned maintenance or refurbishment associated with a Service Asset and which is reasonably necessary to keep the Service Asset operating properly, maintain it, and keep it within regulatory operating compliance so as to ensure that Provider can continue providing the level, nature or manner of Service required under any applicable SLA(s).

 

B-5

“Mexican Law” shall mean any applicable provision of the Constitution of the United Mexican States, any treaty in force in Mexico, any applicable federal law of Mexico or state or municipal law, code, regulation, rule, decree, ordinance, tariff, mandatory Mexican Official Standard, Judgment, injunction, order or other binding legal requirement issued or enacted by a competent Governmental Entity in Mexico, including the applicable laws of the State of Jalisco and the municipality in which the Site is located.

“Ordinary Course of Business” shall mean an action taken by a Person in the ordinary course of the normal day-to-day operations of such Person.

“Party” or “Parties” shall have the meanings set forth in the Preamble.

“Permit Holder” shall have the meaning provided in Section 11.01(a).
