“Prime Rate” shall mean, for any day, the rate of interest per annum last quoted by The Wall Street Journal as the “Prime Rate” in the United States or, if The Wall Street Journal ceases to quote such rate, the “bank prime loan” rate then published by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System in Federal Reserve Statistical Release H.15 entitled “Selected Interest Rates” or any successor publication or, if such rate is no longer published therein, any successor or substantially similar rate published by the Federal Reserve Board. Each change in the Prime Rate shall be effective from and including the date such change is publicly announced or quoted as being effective.

“Pro Rata Share” shall mean with respect to a Service, on any date of determination, a fraction (a) the numerator of which is the level or quantity of such Service consumed or used by Recipient at the Site during the period commencing on the later of (i) the date that is twelve (12) months prior to such date of determination and (ii) the applicable Effective Date, and ending on such date of determination, and (b) the denominator of which is the sum of the level or quantity of such Service consumed or used by all processes (including those of Recipient, Provider and any applicable Third Party) at the Site during such period.

“Provider” shall have the meaning set forth in the Preamble.

“Provider’s Facility” shall mean the land and/or premises owned, licensed, occupied, sub-leased or leased by Provider at the Site (excluding Recipient’s Facility) together with the assets owned by Provider at the Site.

 

B-6

“Reasonable and Prudent Operator” shall mean, with respect to any Service, a Person that (a) to the extent such Service was historically provided at the Site, performs such Service in a manner generally consistent with historical practice with respect to such Service at the Site and (b) to the extent such Service was not historically provided at the Site, exercises the degree of skill, diligence, prudence and foresight reasonably and ordinarily expected of a skilled and experienced provider of services of the same or similar nature under the same or similar circumstances, and, in each case, applies a standard of care no less than that generally applied by Provider in the conduct of its own internal operations.

“Recipient” shall have the meaning set forth in the Preamble.

“Recipient’s Facility” shall mean the premises leased to Recipient under the Guadalajara Lease, together with the assets owned by Recipient and located at such premises and the access, easement, use and other rights granted to Recipient under the Guadalajara Lease that are necessary for Recipient’s occupancy and operations at such premises.

“Release” shall mean any release, spill, emission, discharge, escaping, leaking, pumping, dumping, injection, deposit, disposal, dispersal, leaching or migration or any other release into the indoor or outdoor environment (including ambient air, soil, subsoil, surface water, groundwater and surface or subsurface strata) or into or out of any property, including the movement of Hazardous Material through or in the air, soil, subsoil, surface water, groundwater or property.

“Remediation” means any and all actions required under Environmental Law to: (a) cleanup, remove, treat, restore, contain, abate or remediate Hazardous Materials in the indoor or outdoor environment; (b) prevent or minimize the Release or threatened Release of Hazardous Materials (including by way of vapor intrusion) so that they do not migrate, endanger or threaten to endanger public health or welfare or the indoor or outdoor environment; (c) perform pre-remedial studies, investigations, restoration and post-remedial monitoring studies or post-cleanup care; or (d) respond to requests of any Governmental Entity for information or documents in any way relating to the investigation, monitoring, cleanup, removal, treatment or remediation or potential investigation, monitoring, cleanup, removal, treatment or remediation of Hazardous Materials in the indoor or outdoor environment.

“Required Notice Period” shall mean, with respect to a termination of a Service by Recipient pursuant to Section 6.01, the notice period specified in the applicable SLA or, if no such period is specified, six (6) months. Provider shall have no voluntary termination right pursuant to Section 6.01 unless the applicable SLA expressly provides such a right, in which case the “Required Notice Period” applicable to Provider shall be the notice period expressly specified therein.

“Response Action” shall mean any investigation, remediation or other response action addressing a Release.

“Sales Taxes” shall mean all sales, use, value added, consumption, service, goods and services, excise or similar Taxes, however denominated and any duties, imposts, charges, fees or other levies of whatever nature assessed on the provision of the Services, including any interest and any penalties, fines, additions to tax or additional interest related thereto. Sales Taxes shall not include any income-based Taxes measured by or imposed on Provider’s net income.

 

B-7

“Service” shall have the meaning provided in Section 2.01(a).

“Service Asset” shall mean, on any date of determination, any asset located at or appurtenant to the Facility and used by Provider on such date to provide a Service to Recipient, including all equipment, fixtures, physical facilities, machinery, inventory, spare parts, supplies, tools and other tangible personal property.

“Service Coordinator” shall have the meaning provided in Section 10.02.

“Service Fees and Expenses” shall have the meaning provided in Section 3.02.

“Service Term” shall have the meaning provided in Section 2.02(b).

“Services-Related Response Action” shall mean a Response Action required to be performed as a result of any matter for which indemnification is required under Section 9.02 of this Agreement.

“Shared Permit” shall have the meaning provided in Section 11.01(a).

“Signing Date” shall have the meaning set forth in the Preamble.

“Site” shall mean the Guadalajara North campus located at Carretera Base Aérea, Zapopan, Jalisco, Mexico, where the Facilities are located.

“SLA” shall mean, for any Service, the relevant document in Schedule A which describes in detail such Service and the specific terms relating thereto, including, as applicable, the Specifications, service levels, Service Term, Monthly Costs and applicable costing method.

“Specification” shall mean the specifications or scope of the Service stated in the relevant section of the applicable SLAs, as those Specifications may be amended from time to time either in accordance with the terms of the relevant Section of such SLAs or by agreement in writing between the Parties.

“Taxes” shall mean all taxes of any kind, and all duties, assessments, levies, impost or other like governmental charges in the nature of a tax, including any federal, state, local or foreign income, estimated, sales, use, ad valorem, receipts, value added, franchise, goods and services, profits, license, withholding, payroll, employment, unemployment, excise, premium, property, customs duty, net worth, capital gains, transfer, stamp, documentary, social security (or similar), disability, excise, severance, stamp, environmental, alternative or add-on minimum, or occupation taxes or de-grouping charges, whether or not disputed, together with all interest, penalties and additions imposed with respect to such amounts.

“Taxing Authority” shall mean any Governmental Entity responsible for the administration, determination, collection, assessment or imposition of any Tax.

 

B-8

“Term of this Agreement” shall have the meaning set forth in Section 2.02(a).

“Third Party” shall mean a Person who is not a Party or an Affiliate of a Party.

“Third Party Claim” shall have the meaning provided in Section 9.03(a).

“VAT” shall mean any value-added, excise, sales, use, goods and services or similar Taxes (including any tax imposed in compliance with the European Council Directive of 28 November 2006 on the common system of value added tax (EC Directive 2006/112) and legislation and regulations supplemental thereto) wherever imposed, together with any interest, penalties and additions imposed with respect thereto.

“Willful Breach” shall mean a material breach of any covenant or agreement set forth in this Agreement that is the consequence of an action or failure to act by a Party that such Party intentionally takes or intentionally fails to take with actual knowledge that such action or failure to act would cause such material breach.

ARTICLE II

SERVICES PROVIDED

Section 2.01 Scope of Service; Standard of Care.

(a) Services Provided. Upon the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement, Provider shall provide, or cause to be provided, to Recipient the services set forth in the SLA (each, a “Service,” and, collectively, the “Services”). Each Service shall be covered by and described in more detail in an SLA attached to and made part of this Agreement, which shall set forth, as applicable, the Specifications, service levels, Service Term, Monthly Costs and applicable costing method. Additional services may be requested and added in accordance with Section 2.01(g)(iii).

(b) Requests for Increase in Service Level under the SLA. In no event shall Recipient be entitled to any increase to the level of Service (including for purposes of expansion of Recipient’s Facility) set forth in the SLA without obtaining the prior written consent of Provider, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed.

(c) Curtailment of Supply. In the event that any Service is not available at the anticipated levels for any reason (including any failure, delay, deficiency or shortfall in performance by Provider in connection with such Service or any Force Majeure), Provider shall apply any necessary curtailment in good faith and on an equitable basis so as to avoid adversely impacting Recipient’s operations relative to any other operations at the Site receiving the same Service, including, to the extent applicable, Provider’s own operations. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to reduce, eliminate or mitigate the source or cause of any such curtailment; provided that neither Provider nor any of its Affiliates shall be required to commence or prosecute any Action against any Person in connection therewith. To the extent reasonably practicable, Provider shall provide Recipient with advance notice of any impending curtailment, and the Parties shall reasonably cooperate to avoid or mitigate the effects of such curtailment in a commercially reasonable manner.

 

B-9

(d) Standard of Care. Subject to the provisions of Article XI and except as otherwise expressly set forth in the applicable SLA, Provider shall perform the Services in a manner generally consistent with, and with the same standard of care as, that of a Reasonable and Prudent Operator, in each case, in accordance with applicable Law and Permits. Except as otherwise expressly set forth in the applicable SLA, and to the extent applicable, Provider shall provide each Service substantially in the same manner and at substantially the same service level as immediately prior to the Distribution. Nothing in this Agreement shall require Provider to favor the business of Recipient over Provider’s own businesses or those of any of Provider’s Affiliates, including any subsidiaries or divisions; provided that the foregoing shall not permit Provider to prioritize its own operations (or those of its Affiliates) over Recipient’s operations in a manner inconsistent with this Agreement or the applicable SLA. Except as otherwise expressly provided in an applicable SLA or Section 2.04, Provider shall not be required to expand the scope of any Service or undertake any new capital project solely for Recipient.

(e) Changes. Without limiting Section 2.03 and Section 2.04, in the event that a Party desires a Change, such Party shall deliver a Change Request to the other Party’s Contract Manager. No Party shall be entitled to any Change without the prior written consent of the other Party, which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed; provided that any request for an Additional Service shall be governed by Section 2.01(g)(iii). The timing for the Parties’ approval or rejection of such Change Requests shall be within a commercially reasonable time period under the circumstances; provided, however, that, with respect to any Change Request required by Law, such period shall be sufficient to meet any applicable deadlines or requirements imposed by Law, provided that the requesting Party has given the other Party reasonable advance notice thereof. If a Change Request is approved, any resulting adjustment to the Monthly Costs or the methodology for determining the Monthly Costs for the affected Service, or any one-time charges or expenses arising from such Change, shall be determined in accordance with the applicable SLA or, to the extent not addressed therein, agreed by the Parties in connection with such Change Request and reflected in an amendment to the applicable SLA. Recipient shall be responsible for any such adjustment, charge or expense so determined or agreed.

(f) Specifications. Without otherwise limiting this Agreement, Section 2.01(d) and Section 2.01(g), Provider shall provide each Service indicated in an SLA to Recipient according to the specific scope and in the scale and description set forth in the SLA, subject to the limitations set forth in such SLA (including as to scope, scale and description). Except as otherwise set forth herein, Recipient shall not be entitled to receive any service, nor shall Recipient be required to purchase or to accept any service, different from that set forth in the respective SLA or as otherwise agreed in writing between the Parties.

(g) Cooperation.

(i) The Parties shall cooperate and use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain all consents from Third Parties that are required in order for Provider to provide the Services to Recipient; provided, however, that Consent Costs shall be borne as expressly provided in the applicable SLA, or, if the applicable SLA does not address such costs, (A) by Provider to the extent such Consent Costs are necessary to provide the applicable Service at the scope and service level then required under the applicable SLA, (B) by Recipient to the extent such Consent Costs arise solely from a Recipient-requested

 

B-10

increase in Service, Change or Additional Service, and (C) otherwise, allocated between the Parties on a reasonable basis to the extent attributable to their respective operations or requested changes. Neither Party shall incur or agree to pay any Consent Cost for which the other Party is responsible under this Agreement without such other Party’s prior written consent, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. In the event that a Third Party consent cannot be entered into or obtained, the Parties shall cooperate and use their respective commercially reasonable efforts to arrange for alternative methods of delivering such Services.

(ii) Each Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with the other Party with respect to the Services, including to minimize the expense, distraction and disturbance to the other Party in connection therewith. Such cooperation shall include: (1) commercially reasonable efforts to execute and deliver such further instruments or documents as may be reasonably requested by the other Party and reasonably necessary to enable such other Party to perform its obligations with respect to the provision or receipt of the Services hereunder, and (2) subject to Section 2.03, commercially reasonable efforts to notify the other Party in advance of any changes to its operating environment or personnel that materially impact, or would reasonably be expected to materially impact, the provision or receipt of any Service, and commercially reasonable efforts to work with the other Party in good faith to minimize the adverse effects of any such changes on the Services.

(iii) Additional Services. Recipient may from time to time request that Provider provide a service not then included in an SLA (an “Additional Service”). Provider shall consider any such request in good faith and shall respond within a commercially reasonable time. Provider shall not be obligated to provide any Additional Service unless the Parties agree in writing on the scope, term and pricing of such Additional Service. If Provider declines the request, or the Parties do not agree on such terms within a commercially reasonable time, Recipient may obtain the requested service from a Third Party, and Provider shall provide commercially reasonable cooperation to facilitate the provision of such service by the Third Party, including reasonable access to those portions of the Site within Provider’s control as reasonably necessary for such purpose. Any such access shall be subject to the applicable access and use requirements set forth in Sections 2.05(c) and (d). Any reasonable, documented out-of-pocket costs incurred by Provider in providing such cooperation shall be borne by Recipient. Such cooperation shall not require Provider to undertake a new capital project, grant any right to occupy or use the Site beyond the access contemplated by this Section, or materially disrupt its operations. If the Parties agree to add an Additional Service, such Additional Service shall be documented in a new SLA added to Schedule A or an amendment to an existing SLA, in each case setting forth its scope, term and applicable pricing terms. Upon execution of the applicable SLA or amendment, such Additional Service shall be deemed a Service for purposes of this Agreement. An Intentionally Omitted Service may be added as a Service under this Agreement only if the Parties expressly agree in writing and amend Schedule B accordingly.

 

B-11

Section 2.02 Term.

(a) Term of Agreement. This Agreement shall become effective on the Signing Date and shall remain in effect until the earlier of: (i) the expiration or termination of all Services as provided in this Agreement or the relevant SLAs and (ii) termination of this Agreement by either Party pursuant to Article VI hereof (the “Term of this Agreement”).

(b) Service Term. The term of each Service shall commence on the Effective Date specified in the applicable SLA and shall continue until the earliest of: (i) the expiration of such Service as provided in the applicable SLA, as such expiration may be extended pursuant to Section 6.03(b), or the earlier termination of such Service as provided in the applicable SLA; (ii) termination of such Service by either Party pursuant to Article VI hereof; and (iii) the expiration or termination of this Agreement (the “Service Term”).

Section 2.03 Change in Operations and Facility Expansions.

(a) Changes by Provider. Provider shall, to the extent reasonably practicable, provide prior written notice to Recipient prior to making any material change or modification in the operation of Provider’s Facility (including any expansion) that would be reasonably likely to: (i) materially and adversely affect Provider’s ability to provide any Service (prior to the termination of such Service hereunder), (ii) materially and adversely affect Recipient’s ability to receive any Service (prior to the termination of such Service hereunder), (iii) result in any material breach of any applicable Law (or of any Permit) relating to the provision or receipt of any Service or (iv) require any material adverse change in any Permit applicable to Recipient in connection with its receipt of any Service; provided that if Provider wishes to make any such changes, modifications or expansions, it shall notify Recipient, and, unless such changes, modifications or expansions are required by Law, a Governmental Entity with jurisdiction, or to avoid a reasonably imminent risk of material harm to Persons or property, Provider shall not, in the case of the foregoing items (i) through (iv), without Recipient’s prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed), make any such changes, modifications or expansions until Provider has taken such steps to reasonably ensure that the changes, modifications or expansions do not result in the foregoing items (i) through (iv); provided, further, that in the event that any such changes, modifications or expansions are required by Law, a Governmental Entity with jurisdiction, or to avoid a reasonably imminent risk of material harm to Persons or property, Provider shall cooperate in good faith with Recipient to use reasonable best efforts to minimize the adverse effect of such changes, modifications or expansions on Recipient’s receipt of the affected Services and, for the avoidance of doubt, Recipient’s prior written consent shall not be required.

(b) Changes by Recipient. Recipient shall, to the extent reasonably practicable, consult with Provider prior to making any material change or modification in the operation of Recipient’s Facility (including any expansion of capacity) that would be reasonably likely to: (i) materially increase Recipient’s demand for any Service; (ii) materially and adversely affect Recipient’s ability to receive any Service (prior to the termination of such Service hereunder); (iii) materially and adversely affect Provider’s ability to provide any Service (prior to the termination of such Service hereunder); (iv) result in any material breach of any applicable Law (or of any Permit) relating to the provision or receipt of any Service; or (v) require any material adverse change in any Permit applicable to Provider in connection with its provision of any Service; provided that if Recipient wishes to make any such changes, modifications or

 

B-12

expansions, it shall notify Provider, and, unless such changes, modifications or expansions are required by Law, a Governmental Entity with jurisdiction, or to avoid a reasonably imminent risk of material harm to Persons or property, it shall not, in the case of the foregoing items (i) through (v), without Provider’s prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed), make any such changes, modifications or expansions until it has taken such steps to reasonably ensure that the changes, modifications or expansions do not result in the foregoing items (i) through (v); provided, further, that in the event that any such changes, modifications or expansions are required by Law, a Governmental Entity with jurisdiction, or to avoid a reasonably imminent risk of material harm to Persons or property, Recipient shall cooperate in good faith with Provider to use reasonable best efforts to minimize the adverse effect of such changes, modifications or expansions on Provider’s provision of the affected Services. Notwithstanding the foregoing, any request by Recipient for an increase in the level of any Service shall also be governed by Section 2.01(b).

Section 2.04 Maintenance Expenditures The Parties recognize that, in the Ordinary Course of Business, operation of the Service Assets will require the incurrence of a certain level of Maintenance Expenditures. Provider shall determine in its reasonable discretion the amount of Maintenance Expenditures that are required to keep the Service Assets operating properly, maintained, and within regulatory operating compliance, and will consult with and consider in good faith any requests from Recipient regarding the foregoing.

Before incurring any non-emergency Maintenance Expenditure for which Provider intends to seek reimbursement from Recipient, Provider shall provide Recipient with reasonable prior written notice describing (i) the proposed work, (ii) the reason such work is necessary, (iii) the estimated cost and anticipated schedule, (iv) any quotes then obtained from Third Parties, and (v) the proposed allocation of such cost among Recipient, Provider and any other users of the applicable Service Asset.

Provider shall fund such Maintenance Expenditures; provided that, except to the extent included in the Monthly Costs or otherwise addressed in the applicable SLA, Recipient shall reimburse Provider for Recipient’s allocable share of such Maintenance Expenditures, determined using the allocation methodology set forth in the applicable SLA for the affected Service or, if no such methodology is specified, Recipient’s Pro Rata Share. Provider shall provide reasonable supporting documentation for any amount to be reimbursed by Recipient, including, as applicable, Third-Party invoices and the calculation of Recipient’s allocable share. Recipient may review and dispute any such reimbursable amount in accordance with Section 5.01(b), Section 3.03 and Section 10.03. To the extent Recipient’s reimbursement includes a Third-Party cost, Recipient shall not be required to reimburse such Third-Party cost until Provider has actually paid it and delivered reasonable evidence of payment.

If Recipient’s allocable share of Maintenance Expenditures for the affected Service, whether individually or in the aggregate during any Calendar Year, would be material in relation to the affected Service, such share shall be reimbursable only with Recipient’s prior written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, such consent shall not be required in the case of an emergency requiring immediate action where obtaining such consent is not reasonably practicable. In such case, Provider shall promptly, and in any event no later than three (3) Business Days after incurring such Maintenance Expenditure, provide Recipient with written notice describing the nature of the

 

B-13

emergency, the action taken, the amount of such Maintenance Expenditure and the basis for determining Recipient’s allocable share thereof, and any such Maintenance Expenditure shall be limited to amounts reasonably necessary to respond to the immediate emergency condition. Recipient may dispute the amount or allocation of any such Maintenance Expenditure in accordance with Section 3.03. No Maintenance Expenditure shall be recovered more than once.

Unless otherwise expressly provided in the applicable SLA, if a Maintenance Expenditure constitutes a capital expenditure for an asset that will remain owned by Provider or another Person after termination of the applicable Service, Recipient shall be responsible only for its allocable share of the portion of such capital expenditure amortized on a straight-line basis over the useful life of the applicable improvement during the remaining Service Term. No return on capital, financing charge, profit or markup shall apply to such capital expenditure unless expressly agreed in the applicable SLA. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Section 2.04 or an applicable SLA, Recipient shall not be required to reimburse any Maintenance Expenditure under this Agreement or an applicable SLA to the extent the Guadalajara Lease allocates the underlying maintenance, repair, replacement, capital expenditure or other property-level cost to the landlord thereunder. Nothing in this Section 2.04 shall modify or affect the rights or obligations of any Person under the Guadalajara Lease.

Section 2.05 Provider Personnel; Access.

(a) In providing the Services, Provider, as it deems necessary or appropriate in its reasonable discretion, may use the personnel and resources of Provider.

(b) Subject to Section 2.06, to the extent reasonably necessary in connection with the provision or receipt of the Services and during the time in which the Services are provided, (i) each Party’s personnel shall be permitted reasonable and timely access during normal business hours to such portions of the other Party’s Facility as are reasonably necessary to observe the other Party’s activities as such activities relate to the Services provided hereunder and (ii) Recipient shall provide Provider personnel (including personnel of any of Provider’s Affiliates, agents or contractors) with reasonable and timely access during normal business hours (except in the event of an emergency) to such portions of Recipient’s Facility, and to such office space, equipment, information, premises, real property, personnel, power, telecommunications systems and circuits, computer systems and other areas and resources therein, in each case, as are reasonably necessary for Provider to perform the applicable Services, including, without limitation, reasonable ingress thereto and egress therefrom and Provider’s installation or repair of any pipes, distribution lines or meters.

(c) In connection with any access to the Site or the other Party’s Facility permitted or required under this Agreement, each Party shall, and shall cause its Affiliates, agents and contractors and their respective personnel to, follow, in all material respects, all bona fide and generally applicable rules, policies and procedures governing access to and use of the Site or such Facility (including applicable EH&S Policies), in each case to the extent communicated to such Party in writing in advance. Any such access shall be subject to applicable Law and Permits and, without otherwise limiting the Parties’ obligations under this Agreement, any applicable restrictions under agreements with Third Parties governing access to or use of the Site or such Facility. While accessing the other Party’s Facility, such personnel shall carry and display appropriate identification to the extent required by the applicable Site security or access procedures.

 

B-14

(d) Each Party receiving access to the other Party’s Facility under this Agreement shall: (i) limit such access to its and its Affiliates’ personnel, agents or contractors who reasonably require such access for the purpose for which such access is permitted or required; (ii) follow, and cause its Affiliates, agents or contractors and their respective personnel to follow, all bona fide rules and procedures for use of such Facility applicable to such access, provided that such rules and procedures are communicated in advance to such Party in writing; (iii) not knowingly access, use, alter, disable or interfere with any information technology, telecommunications or other systems, networks, data or resources of the other Party, except to the extent expressly permitted by the other Party (or expressly contemplated by the applicable SLA or another written agreement between the Parties applicable to such access or use); and (iv) not intentionally damage, disrupt or impair the normal operation of such Facility. Any evidenced damage caused by a Party, its Affiliates, agents or contractors or their respective personnel in the Facility of the other Party shall be repaired to the condition prior to such damage by or on behalf of such Party, in each case, at the damaging Party’s sole cost and expense. Any information obtained in connection with access under this Agreement shall be subject to the confidentiality obligations set forth in Section 13.01.

(e) Mexican Labor and Specialized Services Requirements. Provider shall remain exclusively responsible for the direction, supervision, compensation and employment obligations of the personnel used by Provider, its Affiliates, agents and contractors in providing the Services. Provider shall not make personnel available to Recipient in any manner prohibited by applicable Mexican Law. To the extent that any Service constitutes a specialized service or the execution of specialized works under applicable Mexican labor Law, Provider shall (i) maintain in full force and effect any required registration before the Registry of Providers of Specialized Services or Specialized Works (Padrón de Prestadoras de Servicios Especializados u Obras Especializadas or “REPSE”); (ii) comply with the Administrative Order establishing the general provisions governing the registration of individuals and legal entities that provide specialized services or perform specialized works, as referred to in Article 15 of the Mexican Federal Labor Law, published in the Federal Official Gazette on May 24, 2021; (iii) submit, or cause its Affiliates, agents or contractors, as applicable, to submit, on a four-month basis, the information regarding the agreements entered into with Recipient, as required under applicable Law; (iv) ensure that the applicable SLA identifies the specialized Services to be performed and includes the legal requirements set forth in Article 15-A of the Mexican Social Security Law and Articles 13, 14 and 15 of the Mexican Federal Labor Law, including the approximate number of personnel participating in their performance and their general information; and (v) remain responsible for compliance by its contractors and subcontractors with the foregoing requirements. Nothing in this Section 2.05 shall be construed to authorize any Affiliate, agent, contractor or subcontractor to provide any Service directly to Recipient in lieu of Provider.

Section 2.06 Operations and Laws.

(a) Subject to Article XI, each Party shall, in connection with its provision or receipt of any Service (and its performance of its obligations hereunder), (i) act as a Reasonable and Prudent Operator, (ii) comply, at its sole cost and expense, with all applicable Laws and Permits applicable to such Party’s performance hereunder and (iii) in the event such Party, including Persons acting by, through or under such Party, accesses the other Party’s Facility, comply with the applicable EH&S Policies (and other reasonable health, safety and environmental policies) of the Party whose Facility is being accessed, in each case to the extent communicated to such Party in advance; provided that, in the event of any conflict between such policies and applicable Laws or Permits, applicable Laws or Permits shall control and take precedence.

(b) Neither Party shall be required to perform any of its obligations under this Agreement to the extent that it reasonably determines that performing such obligation would violate any applicable Laws or Permit; provided, however, that the Parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate in good faith to: (i) participate, to the extent reasonably necessary, in any proceeding affecting or relating to the Services with a Governmental Entity and (ii) identify and implement any commercially reasonable changes to the manner or method of providing or receiving an affected Service that are reasonably necessary to allow for such Service to be provided or received in compliance with applicable Laws and Permits (including, where reasonably practicable, an alternative means of providing or receiving such Service). With respect to an Essential Site Service, Provider shall not be excused from performance solely because continued performance requires Provider to obtain, maintain, renew or amend a Permit or other authorization within Provider’s reasonable control; provided that Provider shall not be required to perform in violation of applicable Mexican Law. If the existing manner of providing an Essential Site Service becomes legally prohibited, Provider shall implement, or cause to be implemented, a legally permissible alternative method of providing such Essential Site Service, to the extent reasonably practicable, so as to avoid any material interruption or material reduction in the applicable Specifications, contracted capacity or service level. Recipient shall provide reasonable cooperation in connection therewith.

Section 2.07 Risk of Loss. Risk of loss of, and, as applicable, title to, any goods or other tangible property furnished as (or part of) a Service hereunder shall pass to Recipient at the delivery point(s) specified in the applicable SLA. If no delivery point is specified therein, then the delivery point shall be the point at which such goods (or other tangible property) are delivered to or placed under the control of Recipient or its designee. Before the delivery point, Provider shall bear the risk of loss of such goods (or other tangible property), except to the extent any Losses actually result from Recipient’s Willful Breach of this Agreement, gross negligence or Intentional Misconduct, in which case such Losses shall be borne by Recipient. From and after the delivery point, risk of loss of such goods (or other tangible property) shall be borne by Recipient, except to the extent any Losses actually result from Provider’s Willful Breach of this Agreement, gross negligence or Intentional Misconduct, in which case Provider shall bear such Losses.

Section 2.08 Insurance. During the Term of this Agreement, each Party shall maintain customary insurance appropriate to its activities under this Agreement, including, as applicable, commercial general liability, workers’ compensation (or local equivalent), automobile liability and cyber liability insurance. Any additional Site-specific insurance requirement shall be set forth in the applicable SLA. Upon reasonable request, a Party shall provide evidence of the required coverage.

Section 2.09 Migration From Services.

(a) Planning for Migration. Upon the giving of notice of termination of an SLA or, if permitted under the relevant SLA, a separable and distinct portion of the Service under an SLA, or, in the case of the scheduled expiration of an SLA, upon Recipient’s reasonable request made not more than ninety (90) days prior to such expiration, the Parties shall work together in good faith and use commercially reasonable efforts to facilitate an orderly termination or expiration of, and transition away from the providing and receiving of, the applicable Service (or portion thereof). At Recipient’s reasonable request, the Parties shall develop a written transition plan identifying the material phases and milestones, the expected involvement of each Party, known service dependencies and other material transition activities. Provider shall provide the transition assistance described in Section 2.09(b) during the period commencing upon such notice or request and ending ninety (90) days following the effective date of such termination or expiration, unless a different period is set forth in the applicable SLA or otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties.

(b) Provider Transition Assistance. Unless otherwise agreed in writing between the Parties or as specifically set forth in the applicable SLA, Provider shall, to the extent reasonably necessary to facilitate such transition: (1) disclose reasonable information regarding the scope, nature, processes and manner of providing the applicable Service, as then provided; (2) furnish, to the extent then available, records and data relating to Recipient’s receipt of the applicable Service that have been retained by Provider, in accordance with its ordinary records retention policies, in the format and media in which Provider then maintains such data and records; (3) make personnel with relevant knowledge of the applicable Service reasonably available for knowledge transfer and to assist with transition planning and coordination; (4) provide Recipient and its replacement service provider with reasonable access to systems, tools and interfaces used in providing the applicable Service, solely to the extent reasonably necessary to facilitate the transition and subject to the applicable access, use and confidentiality requirements of this Agreement, including Sections 2.05(c) and (d) hereof; and (5) provide such other commercially reasonable cooperation as may be reasonably necessary to facilitate the transition of the applicable Service.

(c) Transition Cost. Except to the extent included in the Monthly Costs or otherwise provided in the relevant SLA, any reasonable, documented costs incurred by Provider in providing the transition assistance described in Section 2.09(b) shall be borne by Recipient; provided that, if Recipient terminates the applicable Service or SLA pursuant to Section 6.02(a) as a result of Provider’s uncured material breach, Provider shall bear such costs.

ARTICLE III

COMPENSATION; INVOICING; AUDITS

Section 3.01 Consideration; Taxes

(a) Monthly Costs. As consideration for Provider providing the Services to Recipient in accordance with this Agreement, Recipient shall pay (or cause to be paid) to Provider, in accordance with this Article III and the applicable SLA, (i) the Monthly Costs applicable to each Service, as set forth in or determined in accordance with the applicable SLA, and (ii) any other amounts expressly payable by Recipient under this Agreement or the applicable

 

B-17

SLA. To the extent the applicable SLA provides that the Monthly Costs for a Service are based on the actual costs attributable to providing such Service, such Monthly Costs shall include only reasonable, documented costs directly attributable to such Service and, with respect to any cost attributable in part to such Service and in part to other activities, the portion thereof reasonably allocable to such Service in accordance with the allocation methodology set forth in the applicable SLA. No amount shall be recovered more than once, and no profit or markup shall be included in the Monthly Costs unless expressly provided in the applicable SLA.

(b) Taxes.

(i) All amounts payable under or in connection with this Agreement, in particular the Monthly Costs referred to in Section 3.01(a) for the Services, are exclusive of any Sales Taxes and VAT.

(ii) Where a payment under or in connection with this Agreement constitutes the consideration for a supply (or the equivalent) for VAT purposes, or in case a supply or service under or in connection with this Agreement is subject to VAT, then each Party shall pay to the relevant Taxing Authority VAT in an amount owed by it as determined in accordance with applicable VAT Laws. Each Party shall issue to the respective other Party a valid VAT invoice (or the equivalent) in compliance with applicable VAT Laws in respect thereof. To the extent that a reverse charge procedure applies, the receiving Party shall not be required to pay (or cause to be paid) any amount in respect of that VAT to the other Party (but rather pay such VAT directly to the applicable Taxing Authority).

(iii) Where one Party is liable to (or to cause one of its Affiliates to) indemnify or reimburse another Party (or one of that Party’s Affiliates) under the terms of or in connection with this Agreement in respect of any amount, including any costs, charges or expenses, the indemnity or reimbursement payment will include an amount equal to any VAT on those costs, charges or expenses that is not otherwise recoverable (as demonstrated by the non-recovering Party) by the other Party (or its Affiliate) or the representative member of any VAT group of which it forms part, subject to that person or representative member using commercially reasonable efforts to recover such amount of VAT.

(iv) Recipient shall pay or reimburse Provider for any and all Sales Taxes (other than VAT, which the Parties agree shall be dealt with pursuant to Section 3.01(b)(ii) and Section 3.01(b)(iii) above) on the provision of the Services imposed on Provider (or any of its Affiliates) or which Provider shall have any obligation to collect with respect to or relating to this Agreement or the performance by Provider of its obligations hereunder. Provider shall calculate such Sales Taxes in good faith consultation with Recipient. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Recipient agrees to use commercially reasonable efforts to provide exemption certificates or other documentation where available or to make payment of Sales Taxes directly to the appropriate Taxing Authority. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary herein, Recipient shall not be responsible for any penalties or interest to the extent attributable to Provider’s failure to timely remit any Sales Taxes or VAT to the applicable Taxing Authority after receipt thereof from Recipient.

 

B-18

(v) Neither Party (nor any of its Affiliates) shall deduct or withhold any Taxes from any amounts payable pursuant to this Agreement unless such deduction or withholding of Taxes is required under applicable Law. If any applicable Law requires the deduction or withholding of any Tax from any such payments then Provider or Recipient (or any of their respective Affiliates), as the case may be, shall (1) be entitled to make such deduction or withholding, (2) timely pay the full amount deducted or withheld to the relevant Taxing Authority in accordance with applicable Law and (3) provide the other Party with a receipt or other documentation evidencing such payment, including the amount paid and the applicable Taxing Authority to which payment was made. Each Party agrees to use (and to cause its Affiliates to use) reasonable efforts to furnish such forms, certificates or other documentation, upon the reasonable request of the other Party, that would reduce or eliminate such deduction or withholding, and each Party shall (and shall cause its Affiliates to) reasonably cooperate with the other Party to minimize any such deduction or withholding.

(c) Emergency Expenses. In the event of an emergency that materially interrupts, or is reasonably expected to materially interrupt, Recipient’s receipt of a Service, Provider may incur reasonable, documented expenses not included in the Monthly Costs or otherwise provided for in the applicable SLA that are reasonably necessary to prevent or mitigate such interruption or restore the affected Service; provided that, to the extent reasonably practicable under the circumstances, Provider shall obtain Recipient’s prior written consent before incurring any such expenses. If obtaining such consent is not reasonably practicable because the emergency requires immediate action, Provider may incur such expenses without prior consent, but only to the extent reasonably necessary to address the immediate consequences of such emergency on Recipient’s receipt of the affected Service.

Provider shall promptly, and in any event no later than three (3) Business Days after incurring any such expenses without Recipient’s prior written consent, provide Recipient with written notice describing the nature of the emergency, the actions taken, the amount of such expenses and the basis for determining the portion thereof attributable to Recipient. Recipient shall reimburse Provider only for the portion of such expenses reasonably attributable to Recipient’s receipt of the affected Service. Recipient may dispute the amount or allocation of any such expense in accordance with Section 3.03(b). Recipient shall not be required to reimburse any such expense until Provider has incurred the expense and delivered reasonable supporting documentation then available, including applicable Third-Party invoices or receipts and the calculation of Recipient’s allocable share.

Costs arising from Provider’s failure to perform required maintenance or comply with applicable Law or Permits shall not be reimbursable as emergency expenses under this Section 3.01(c), except to the extent expressly provided in the applicable SLA. For the avoidance of doubt, any expense that constitutes a Maintenance Expenditure shall be governed by Section 2.04. Nothing in this Section 3.01(c) is intended to alter the allocation of environmental liabilities or responsibilities under Article IX or the Separation Agreement. No emergency expense payable hereunder shall be recovered more than once.

Section 3.02 Invoices; Mexican Tax Compliance.

(a) Invoices. Unless otherwise provided in the applicable SLA, Provider shall issue, on a monthly basis, an electronic tax invoice (Comprobante Fiscal Digital por Internet) (“CFDI”) for the Services provided in the applicable month. Each CFDI shall comply with Articles 29 and 29-A of the Mexican Federal Tax Code (Código Fiscal de la Federación) and all other requirements of applicable Mexican Law and shall include all information and tax complements (Complementos Fiscales) required thereunder, including the payment complement (Complemento de Pago), where applicable. Provider shall provide invoices for the Services provided in the applicable month no later than forty-five (45) days following the last day of such month. Invoices shall set forth the Monthly Costs, Taxes (including Sales Taxes) and any other amounts expressly payable by Recipient under this Article III or the applicable SLA (collectively, “Service Fees and Expenses”), if any, for the applicable billing period. Such invoices shall designate the amount invoiced in respect of each SLA. On a monthly basis, Provider shall designate currency conversion rates, which Provider shall reasonably determine based on the Applicable Exchange Rate, on the last day of the month in which the Service is provided.

(b) Mexican Tax Compliance. Provider represents and warrants that it is not, and has not been, included in any list published by the Mexican Tax Administration Service (Servicio de Administración Tributaria) (“SAT”) under Articles 69 or 69-B of the Mexican Federal Tax Code (Código Fiscal de la Federación). Provider shall provide to the Recipient, on a timely basis, an updated tax compliance opinion (Opinión de Cumplimiento) issued by SAT and a tax situation certificate (Constancia de Situación Fiscal). If Provider becomes listed under Article 69 or 69-B of the Mexican Federal Tax Code, the Provider shall immediately notify Recipient in writing and provide all documentation reasonably necessary to demonstrate that the Services under the applicable SLA were actually rendered. Provider shall indemnify and hold harmless Recipient from and against any Taxes, fines, surcharges, inflation adjustments, interest or other amounts that Recipient is required to pay to the extent the applicable Mexican Taxing Authority rejects the deduction or the tax credit of payments made to Provider as a result of the application of Article 69 or 69-B of the Mexican Federal Tax Code

Section 3.03 Payments; Audit.

(a) Invoice Remittance; Audit. Recipient shall pay (or cause to be paid) to Provider, on or before thirty (30) days after Recipient’s receipt of such invoice (the “Due Date”), without demand and without any deduction, set-off, withholding or abatement whatsoever (except as provided in Sections 3.01(b)(v), 3.03(b) and 3.03(e)), the full amount of Service Fees and Expenses due unless the amount due is disputed, in which event the dispute shall be resolved in accordance with the terms of Section 3.03(b). All payments hereunder shall be made by electronic funds transmission or other mutually agreeable means denominated in U.S. dollars, except as otherwise specified in the applicable SLA or required by applicable Law. Payments due on a day other than a Business Day shall be due on the next succeeding Business Day. Any undisputed payment not received by Provider on or before the date that is thirty (30) days following the Due Date shall bear interest on the unpaid amount at the Default Rate, accruing daily beginning on the thirty-first (31st) day following the Due Date through and including the date of payment. Recipient may review amounts invoiced and reimbursed pursuant to this Agreement in accordance with Section 5.01(b).

 

B-20

(b) Disputed Amounts. If Recipient, acting in good faith, disputes the accuracy of all or part of any invoice, Recipient shall notify Provider’s Contract Manager promptly, and in any event no later than ninety (90) days following receipt of the invoice in question, setting forth in reasonable detail the basis for such dispute. Any objection to the amount of any invoice shall be deemed to be a Dispute hereunder subject to the provisions applicable to Disputes set forth in Section 10.03. If Recipient does not provide such notice within such ninety (90) day period, Recipient may not thereafter dispute the applicable invoice, except with respect to (i) any adjustment or credit required pursuant to Section 3.03(d), (ii) any clerical or computational error, including any error in applying an allocation methodology expressly set forth in an applicable SLA, or (iii) any overcharge or other invoicing error that could not reasonably have been identified, based on the information reasonably available to Recipient, within such ninety (90) day period.

(c) Payment Default; Discontinuation of Service. If any Service Fees and Expenses that are due and payable to Provider (other than disputed amounts that the Parties are working in good faith to resolve in accordance with Section 3.03(b)) remain unpaid following the expiration of the grace period identified in Section 3.03(a), Provider may notify Recipient in writing of such payment default in accordance with the notice provisions set forth in Section 13.05. Without limiting Recipient’s obligation to pay interest under Section 3.03(a), if Recipient has not cured such payment default within thirty (30) days after Recipient receives such notice, Provider shall have the right, in its sole and absolute discretion, to (i) suspend its provision of any Service to which such unpaid amounts relate until Recipient cures such payment default or (ii) require Recipient to make payment in advance for any Service to which such unpaid amounts relate. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Provider shall not suspend an Essential Site Service pursuant to this Section 3.03(c) except to the extent expressly permitted by the applicable SLA. Provider’s exercise of its rights under this Section 3.03(c) shall be without prejudice to its other rights and remedies under this Agreement, including its termination right under Section 6.02(b).

(d) Reconciliation. Except as otherwise provided in the applicable SLA, to the extent any Monthly Costs invoiced with respect to a Service are based on estimates, forecasts, provisional allocations or other amounts subject to adjustment, Provider shall reconcile such Monthly Costs at least annually against the amounts properly chargeable for such Service under the applicable SLA. Following completion of any such reconciliation, Provider shall issue to Recipient an invoice for any underpayment or credit Recipient for any overpayment. Recipient shall pay any such invoice in accordance with the payment terms of this Agreement, and the amount of any such credit shall be applied by Provider against any amounts next coming due and payable by Recipient to Provider under this Agreement, whether under the applicable SLA or any other SLA, until the full amount of such credit has been so applied; provided that, if no further amounts are reasonably expected to become payable by Recipient to Provider under this Agreement, Provider shall pay any remaining unapplied amount of such credit to Recipient within thirty (30) days following completion of the applicable reconciliation.

(e) No Offset. Regardless of any other rights under any agreements, neither Provider nor Recipient shall have the right to set-off the amount of any Claim (or part of any such amount) it may have under this Agreement, whether contingent or otherwise, against any amount owed by such Party to another Party, whether under this Agreement or otherwise; provided, however, that a Party may set off against amounts otherwise payable by such Party under

this Agreement any amount owed to such Party by the other Party under this Agreement that has been (i) expressly agreed in writing by the Parties to be due and payable or (ii) finally determined to be due and payable pursuant to the dispute resolution procedures set forth in Section 10.03. For the avoidance of doubt, the application of any credit expressly provided for under this Agreement or an applicable SLA shall not constitute a set-off prohibited by this Section 3.03(e).

ARTICLE IV

INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

Section 4.01 Intellectual Property.

(a) Intellectual Property Ownership. Subject to Section 4.01(b), nothing in this Agreement (including the performance, provision, use or receipt of the Services) will be deemed to transfer, assign or otherwise convey any right, title or interest in or to any Intellectual Property or data of one Party or its Affiliates to the other Party or its Affiliates. As of the Signing Date, neither Party intends to jointly develop any Intellectual Property under this Agreement or develop any Intellectual Property on behalf of the other under this Agreement. If the Parties at any time anticipate such development of Intellectual Property under this Agreement, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith an agreement regarding their respective Intellectual Property rights arising from such development prior to the commencement thereof.

(b) Grant of License. Subject to the terms and conditions of this Agreement, each Party, on behalf of itself and its Affiliates, hereby grants to the other Party and its Affiliates a non-exclusive, nontransferable, except pursuant to a permitted assignment of this Agreement, worldwide, royalty-free license, during the applicable Service Term and, solely to the extent necessary to complete any orderly wind-down or migration activities contemplated by this Agreement, for a reasonable period thereafter, to use the Intellectual Property, other than trademarks and other source indicators, owned by such Party or its Affiliates solely to the extent necessary for and solely for the purposes of performing obligations under this Agreement, providing, receiving or using the Services in accordance with this Agreement, or completing such wind-down or migration. The foregoing license may be sublicensed only to the receiving Party’s Affiliates and to its and their contractors, service providers, advisors and representatives who have a need to use such Intellectual Property for the purposes permitted by this Section 4.01(b) and who are subject to confidentiality and use restrictions consistent with this Agreement. Neither Party shall use the other Party’s Intellectual Property for any purpose other than as expressly permitted by this Agreement, and no rights or licenses are granted by implication, exhaustion or otherwise.

ARTICLE V

RECORDS; FORECASTS

Section 5.01 Records.

(a) Records. Each Party agrees to maintain financial, accounting and functional (including metering) records, data and other supporting documentation consistent with its practices in the Ordinary Course of Business to reflect the accuracy of invoiced quantities and amounts applicable to the Services provided under this Agreement. Each Party shall retain such data and records in accordance with its respective control policies in the Ordinary Course of Business existing from time to time.

(b) Review of Charges. Upon reasonable prior written notice, Provider shall make available to Recipient, during normal business hours, such books, records and supporting documentation as are reasonably necessary to verify the calculation of Service Fees and Expenses. Any such review shall be conducted at Recipient’s expense, in a manner that does not unreasonably interfere with Provider’s operations and subject to the confidentiality provisions of Section 13.01. Any Dispute arising from such review shall be subject to Section 3.03(b) and resolved in accordance with Section 10.03.

Section 5.02 Annual Service Forecast. Subject to the terms of any SLA, during the Term of this Agreement, the Contract Managers (and such other representatives as they may designate) shall, at least annually and, to the extent reasonably practicable, sufficiently in advance of the commencement of each succeeding Calendar Year, discuss in good faith the anticipated scope, nature, level and quantity of Services to be provided by Provider in such succeeding Calendar Year. In connection with such discussion, Provider shall also provide Recipient with a good faith estimate of any material Maintenance Expenditures reasonably anticipated to be allocable to Recipient during such succeeding Calendar Year. If the Parties do not agree on any proposed change arising from such discussion, the applicable SLA will remain in effect in accordance with its terms. For the avoidance of doubt, no change to any Specification, Service Term, Monthly Costs or other term of an SLA shall be effective unless documented in accordance with Section 2.01(e), Section 2.01(g)(iii), or Section 13.04, as applicable.

ARTICLE VI

TERMINATION

Section 6.01 Voluntary Termination of a Service. Recipient may terminate any Service by giving Provider written notice that satisfies the Required Notice Period applicable to Recipient for such Service. Provider may voluntarily terminate a Service only to the extent expressly permitted by the applicable SLA and upon satisfaction of the Required Notice Period, if any, that applies to Provider thereunder. Unless otherwise expressly provided in the applicable SLA, termination of any Service shall be effective only on the last day of a calendar month and, subject to Section 2.01(e), each Service must be terminated in whole, and not in part. The notice of termination of any Service shall be (a) sufficiently specific as to identify the particular Service for which any such termination shall apply and (b) irrevocable upon receipt by the other Party. Termination of a Service pursuant to this Section 6.01 shall not relieve Recipient of its obligation to pay any amounts properly due with respect to such Service through the effective date of termination. Following receipt of a notice of termination from Recipient, Provider shall not be required to make any capital expenditure or enter into any new Third Party commitment attributable solely to periods following the effective date of such termination, except to the extent reasonably necessary to continue providing the applicable Service in accordance with this Agreement through such effective date. Any voluntary termination right granted to Provider in an SLA with respect to an Essential Site Service shall be subject to Recipient’s prior written consent or the availability, as of the effective date of such termination, of a substitute service reasonably equivalent in all material respects that is legally available and fully operational and, to the extent applicable to the nature of such Essential Site Service, physically connected and tested.

Section 6.02 Early Termination.

(a) Default. Subject to the terms of Article XII, and except for a payment default (which shall be governed by Section 6.02(b)), if a Party (the “Defaulting Party”) shall fail to perform or defaults in any material respect in the performance of any of its obligations under this Agreement or an applicable SLA, the other Party (the “Non-Defaulting Party”) may give written notice to the Defaulting Party specifying the nature of such failure or default and stating that the Non-Defaulting Party intends to terminate the applicable Service or applicable SLA if such failure or default is not cured within thirty (30) days following receipt of such notice. If such failure or default cannot reasonably be cured within such thirty (30)-day period, the cure period shall be extended for such time as reasonably necessary to complete the cure, provided that the Defaulting Party commences such cure within the initial thirty (30)-day period and diligently pursues the same to completion. If such failure or default is not cured within the applicable cure period, the Non-Defaulting Party may terminate the applicable Service or applicable SLA upon written notice to the Defaulting Party. Any termination pursuant to this Section 6.02(a) shall be without prejudice to any other remedy that may be available to the Non-Defaulting Party.

(b) Payment Default. If Recipient fails to cure a payment default in accordance with Section 3.03(c) hereof, Provider may terminate, upon written notice to Recipient, the applicable Service or applicable SLA to which such payment default relates. Provider’s exercise of such termination right shall be without prejudice to its other rights and remedies under this Agreement.

(c) Other Termination Rights. In addition to any other rights or remedies of the Parties under this Agreement, either Provider or Recipient may, to the extent permitted by Law, terminate this Agreement with immediate effect upon written notice to the other Party upon the occurrence of any of the following events:

(i) the admitted insolvency of such other Party;

(ii) the institution by such other Party of any voluntary proceeding in bankruptcy, insolvency, moratorium, receivership, winding-up, dissolution or reorganization, or the institution of any such involuntary proceeding against such other Party that is not dismissed or stayed within sixty (60) days; or

(iii) if, in connection with the performance of this Agreement, such other Party violates the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act of 1977, the U.K. Bribery Act of 2010 or any other applicable anti-bribery, anti-corruption, anti-money laundering or sanctions Laws of any jurisdiction, in each case, that would reasonably be expected to expose the terminating Party (or any of its Affiliates) to material legal or regulatory liability.

 

B-24

(d) Loss of Site Rights. Provider shall not voluntarily relinquish or permit the expiration or termination of any ownership, leasehold, license, access or other right within Provider’s control that is necessary to provide an Essential Site Service unless, before such relinquishment, expiration or termination becomes effective, Provider has made commercially reasonable arrangements to preserve the continued lawful provision of such Essential Site Service. Subject to the foregoing and unless an SLA expressly provides otherwise, if either Party ceases to have any legal right (whether by ownership, leasehold, license or otherwise) necessary to occupy or operate the applicable Facility and, as a result, the continued provision or receipt of a Service is no longer legally permissible (or reasonably practicable), such Service or applicable SLA (as applicable) shall terminate as of the date that such legal right ceases; provided that no such termination shall occur solely as a result of any assignment or transfer permitted under Section 13.02 to a Person that has the legal rights necessary to occupy or operate the applicable Facility and assumes the applicable obligations hereunder.

Section 6.03 Effect of Termination.

(a) Cessation. Recipient specifically agrees and acknowledges that all obligations of Provider to provide each respective Service shall immediately cease upon the expiration or earlier termination of the Service Term for such Service. Provider shall have no obligation to recommence the provision of any Service to Recipient once any Service terminates under this Agreement. Further, upon the cessation of Provider’s obligation to provide any Service under this Agreement or the applicable SLA, Recipient shall immediately cease using, directly or indirectly, such Service (including any and all Provider software or third-party software provided through Provider and computer systems or equipment). Subject to the terms of any SLA, if Recipient continues to use any Service beyond such date, Recipient shall be responsible to Provider for such continued use, including any Third Party costs incurred by Provider as a result thereof, to the extent not otherwise included in the charges described below. For the first ten (10) days following such date, the charges for such continued use shall equal the Service Fees and Expenses that would have been payable for such Service had the applicable Service Term continued. Thereafter, the charges for such continued use shall equal one hundred ten percent (110%) of the Monthly Costs that would have been payable for such Service had the applicable Service Term continued, plus any other Service Fees and Expenses attributable to such continued use. The foregoing shall not apply during any extension period pursuant to Section 6.03(b), and the charges during any such extension period shall instead be determined in accordance therewith.

(b) Exit Support; Service Extensions. Unless otherwise expressly provided in the applicable SLA, if Recipient reasonably determines that it will require an Essential Site Service, or another Service expressly designated in the applicable SLA as eligible for extension under this Section 6.03(b), to continue beyond the expiration of the then-current Service Term, Recipient may, by written notice to Provider delivered at least thirty (30) days prior to such expiration, extend the Service Term for an additional period of three (3) months. Recipient may thereafter extend the Service Term for up to two additional successive periods of three (3) months each by providing Provider with at least thirty (30) days’ prior written notice of each such extension. Subject to applicable Law, Provider shall continue to provide such Service during each such extension period in accordance with this Agreement and the applicable SLA. The pricing applicable during each such extension period shall be as agreed in writing by the Parties; provided that, if the Parties have not agreed in writing on alternative pricing prior to the commencement of the applicable extension period, the Monthly Costs shall be the Monthly Costs that would otherwise have been payable for such Service had the applicable Service Term continued. In each case, any other Service Fees and Expenses shall continue to apply in accordance with this Agreement and the applicable SLA. Any extension of a Service not eligible for extension under this Section 6.03(b), and any further extension beyond the periods described above, shall be subject to mutual written agreement of the Parties.

Section 6.04 Survival of Payment Obligations. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein, the termination of this Agreement or any SLA shall not affect Recipient’s obligation to pay any amount then owed to Provider (and amounts that become due and payable pursuant to the terms hereof after the applicable termination date) or a Third Party hereunder, including, solely to the extent expressly provided in the applicable SLA, any reasonable, documented and unavoidable costs incurred by Provider as a direct result of such termination.

Section 6.05 Settlement of Accounts. Upon termination of this Agreement or any SLA, the Parties shall take all steps as may reasonably be required to complete any final settlement of accounts owing hereunder between them with respect to this Agreement or such SLA. Upon the termination of this Agreement, there will be a final accounting and each Party shall pay to the other Party any amounts owed to the other Party in accordance with the payment terms set forth in this Agreement.

ARTICLE VIII

LIMITATION OF LIABILITY

Section 8.01 Liability. Subject to Section 8.03, the aggregate Liability of each Party (and its Affiliates) to the other Party (and its Affiliates) for any Claims or Losses that arise under this Agreement and relate to the provision or receipt of any Service shall not exceed, with respect to the affected Service or Services, the aggregate Service Fees and Expenses paid (or payable) for such affected Service or Services during the twelve (12)-month period immediately prior to the event giving rise to such Claim or Loss; provided that, if any affected Service has been provided for less than twelve (12) months as of such event, the amount attributable to such Service for purposes of this Section 8.01 shall be the amount of Service Fees and Expenses that would reasonably be expected to be paid or payable for such Service during the first twelve (12) months of its Service Term, based on the then-current Monthly Costs and other applicable charges. The foregoing sentence shall not limit Recipient’s obligation to pay Service Fees and Expenses or other amounts due under this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, this Article VIII applies only to Liabilities arising under this Agreement and shall not limit or otherwise affect any Liability arising under the Separation Agreement or under any other Ancillary Agreement.

Section 8.02 Limitation of Losses. SUBJECT TO SECTION 8.03, IN NO EVENT SHALL THE PARTIES OR THEIR RESPECTIVE AFFILIATES BE LIABLE FOR PUNITIVE, EXEMPLARY, SPECIAL, INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL LOSSES ARISING FROM OR RELATING TO ANY CLAIM MADE UNDER THIS AGREEMENT OR REGARDING THE PROVISION OR RECEIPT OF OR THE FAILURE TO PROVIDE OR RECEIVE SERVICE(S) HEREUNDER (EXCEPT FOR ALL COMPONENTS OF AWARDS AGAINST THE NON-BREACHING PARTY IN ANY THIRD PARTY CLAIM, INCLUDING COMPONENTS OF SUCH THIRD PARTY CLAIM RELATING TO ANY OF THE FOREGOING AND ATTORNEYS’ FEES).

Section 8.03 Exceptions to Limitation of Liability; Enhanced Cap.

(a) Uncapped Liabilities. Notwithstanding Sections 8.01 and 8.02, the limitations of Liability and Losses set forth therein shall not apply to any Claim or Loss to the extent arising from fraud, gross negligence, Willful Breach or Intentional Misconduct, and any such Claim or Loss shall not be subject to any liability cap under this Article VIII.

(b) Enhanced Cap Liabilities. Subject to Section 8.03(a), with respect to any Claim or Loss arising from or relating to (i) fines or penalties, including the revocation of any Permit, assessed by a Governmental Entity, (ii) any obligation to indemnify, defend and hold harmless under Article IX with respect to any Third Party Claim, (iii) a breach of Section 13.01 or applicable data-protection or data-security obligations or (iv) the provision or receipt of any Critical Service, Sections 8.01 and 8.02 shall not otherwise limit recovery; provided that the aggregate Liability of each Party and its Affiliates for such Claims and Losses shall not exceed three (3) times the amount that would otherwise constitute the applicable liability cap under Section 8.01 (the “Enhanced Cap”). If and to the extent any Claim or Loss described in this Section 8.03(b) also arises from fraud, gross negligence, Willful Breach, or Intentional Misconduct, Section 8.03(a) shall control and such Claim or Loss shall not be subject to the Enhanced Cap or any other liability cap under this Article VIII.

(c) Separate Liability Allocations. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Article VIII, nothing in this Article VIII shall limit, modify or otherwise affect any Liability or responsibility allocated pursuant to the Separation Agreement or Section 9.02.

Section 8.04 SLA-Specific Liability Provisions. An applicable SLA may designate a Service as a Critical Service and set forth liability caps, limitations and remedies applicable to the Services covered thereby. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Article VIII, such provisions of the applicable SLA shall govern with respect to those Services.

Section 8.05 Mitigation. Recipient or Provider (as the case may be) shall use its commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the Losses (if any) that it incurs as a result of any breach by the other Party of such other Party’s obligations under this Agreement.

ARTICLE IX

INDEMNIFICATION

Section 9.01 Indemnification.

(a) Indemnification by Recipient. Recipient shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Provider and its Affiliates from and against any and all Losses to the extent arising out of, relating to or resulting from (i) Recipient’s (or any of its Affiliates’) material breach of this Agreement, (ii) the gross negligence or Intentional Misconduct of Recipient or any of its Affiliates in connection with the receipt or use of the Services, (iii) Recipient’s (or any of its Affiliates’) failure to comply with applicable Law or any Permit in connection with the receipt or use of the Services, (iv) Recipient’s (or any of its Affiliates’) use of the Services other than in accordance with this Agreement, or (v) the negligence of Recipient or any of its Affiliates in connection with the receipt or use of any Critical Service, other than any matter governed by Section 9.02.

(b) Indemnification by Provider. Provider shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Recipient and its Affiliates from and against any and all Losses to the extent arising out of, relating to or resulting from (i) Provider’s (or any of its Affiliates’) material breach of this Agreement, (ii) the gross negligence or Intentional Misconduct of Provider or any of its Affiliates in connection with the provision of the Services, (iii) Provider’s (or any of its Affiliates’) failure to comply with applicable Law or any Permit in connection with the provision of the Services, or (iv) the negligence of Provider or any of its Affiliates in connection with the provision of any Critical Service, other than any matter governed by Section 9.02.
