Section 9.02 Environmental Indemnification.

(a) Subject to the Separation Agreement, this Section 9.02 shall govern the allocation under this Agreement of responsibility of each Party for Losses relating to or arising out of Environmental Laws or any Permit required by or issued pursuant to any Environmental Law (“Environmental Permits”) that relate to the provision or receipt of any Services hereunder. Nothing in this Section 9.02 shall alter the allocation of environmental liabilities or responsibilities under the Separation Agreement, which shall control to the extent applicable.

(b) Provider shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Recipient and its Affiliates from and against any and all Losses, including all cost and expenses of any Remediation or Response Action, related to the provision or receipt (or non-provision or non-receipt) of Services hereunder after the applicable Effective Date that:

(i) arise from Provider’s failure to comply with applicable Environmental Laws or Environmental Permits, including any failure by Provider to obtain, maintain, renew or comply with any Environmental Permit required for the provision of the Services; or

(ii) arise from a Release of Hazardous Materials at the Site caused by Provider or its employees, agents, contractors, subcontractors, licensees or invitees or attributable to Provider’s operations on or after the applicable Effective Date, except to the extent the same constitutes a Liability for which Recipient or any of its Affiliates are responsible pursuant to the terms of the Separation Agreement.

(c) Recipient shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Provider and its Affiliates from and against any and all Losses related to the provision or receipt (or non-provision or non-receipt) of Services hereunder after the applicable Effective Date that:

(i) arise from Recipient’s failure to comply with applicable Environmental Laws or Environmental Permits; or

(ii) arise from a Release of Hazardous Materials at the Site caused by Recipient or its employees, agents, contractors, subcontractors, licensees or invitees or attributable to Recipient’s operations on or after the applicable Effective Date, except to the extent the same constitutes a Liability for which Provider or any of its Affiliates are responsible pursuant to the terms of the Separation Agreement.

(d) Where, in connection with acts or omissions of the nature referred to in Section 9.02(b) or Section 9.02(c) above, both Provider and Recipient (including their respective officers, directors, employees, contractors, agents or invitees) have jointly caused any Losses, whether or not a Third Party’s acts or omissions also were causal, Recipient and Provider shall contribute to their common liability a pro rata share based upon the relative degree of fault of each (including attorneys’ fees and other costs of defense) in connection with the acts or omissions giving rise to such Losses; provided that, with respect to Losses arising due to events, actions or occurrences occurring prior to the applicable Effective Date, the Liability of Provider and Recipient for such Losses shall be allocated in accordance with the terms of the Separation Agreement. In a case where the Parties are both liable for jointly caused Losses, the Parties shall

initially share all costs in proportion to their estimated relative degrees of fault (or, if such relative degrees of fault cannot reasonable be estimated at that time equally) (including attorneys’ fees and other costs of defense, if the Parties choose common counsel), but if either Party selects its own counsel, such Party shall initially bear its own attorneys’ fees and costs of defense; provided that either Party may, based on reasonably available evidence, request that the foregoing costs be provisionally allocated based on the Parties’ estimated relative degrees of fault, and the Parties shall promptly confer in good faith regarding such provisional allocation. Any provisional allocation agreed in writing by the Parties shall apply pending final allocation and shall be subject to reimbursement or reallocation once (i) there is a final Judgment allocating fault between Provider and Recipient or (ii) Provider and Recipient otherwise agree in writing to a final allocation of fault between them. If the Parties do not agree to a provisional allocation within ten (10) Business Days after such request, either Party may submit the matter for resolution in accordance with Section 10.03. Until such provisional allocation is agreed or otherwise determined, the foregoing initial cost sharing shall continue. Upon such final determination or agreement, the Parties shall make such payments or reimbursements as are necessary to reflect the applicable final allocation of fault.

(e) For purposes of clarification, the indemnification obligations of Provider and Recipient with respect to occurrences, events, actions, omissions, violations of Environmental Laws or Environmental Permits, or Releases of Hazardous Materials that occurred prior to the applicable Effective Date, shall be governed by the terms of the Separation Agreement.

Section 9.03 Indemnification Procedures.

(a) The indemnification procedures set forth in Section 6.4 and Section 6.5 of the Separation Agreement shall apply, mutatis mutandis, to claims for indemnification under this Article IX. For purposes of this Article IX, any Person entitled to indemnification hereunder is an “Indemnified Party,” the Party obligated to provide such indemnification is an “Indemnifying Party,” and any claim or demand asserted by a Third Party against an Indemnified Party which gives (or would reasonably be expected to give) rise to a right of indemnification hereunder is a “Third Party Claim.” The procedures related to indemnification of Tax matters shall be exclusively governed by the Tax Matters Agreement. Nothing in this Section 9.03 shall expand the substantive indemnification obligations set forth in this Article IX.

(b) Notwithstanding Section 9.03(a) above, to the extent a Services-Related Response Action affects (or has the potential to affect) any other Response Action that is being (or is anticipated to be) performed by the Indemnified Party, the Indemnified Party shall have the right, but not the obligation, to perform such Services-Related Response Action as well. In such case, the Indemnified Party shall keep the Indemnifying Party reasonably informed of the progress of the Services-Related Response Action.

ARTICLE X

MANAGEMENT AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION

Section 10.01 Contract Managers.

(a) Each Party shall appoint a Contract Manager, who shall be responsible for all day-to-day operational and administrative matters arising hereunder and shall be the primary contact for the other Party for any issues arising hereunder (each, a “Contract Manager”). The initial Contract Managers shall be [•] for Recipient and [•] for Provider. Each Party may change its designated Contract Manager at any time upon reasonable prior written notice to the other Party.

(b) The Contract Managers shall meet (in person or by audio or video conference) on a regular basis and no less frequently than quarterly (and more frequently upon either Party’s reasonable request) during the Term of this Agreement in order to facilitate the provision and receipt of the Services in accordance with this Agreement and the orderly transition of the Services at the end of the applicable Service Term. During such meetings, the Contract Managers may, among other things, discuss invoices, requests for Changes or additional Services and any other issues requiring coordination or resolution under this Agreement.

Section 10.02 Service Coordinators. With respect to each Service, each Party shall appoint a service-specific coordinator, who shall be responsible for all day-to-day operational and administrative matters arising under such Service and shall be the primary contact for the other Party for issues arising under that specific Service (each, a “Service Coordinator”). Each Party may change any Service Coordinator upon notice to the other Party. The same individual may serve as Service Coordinator for more than one Service and may also be a Contract Manager, provided that the required responsibilities can be performed effectively.

Section 10.03 Dispute Resolution.

(a) Except as otherwise expressly provided in an SLA, the dispute resolution procedures set forth in Article VIII of the Separation Agreement shall apply and are hereby incorporated herein by reference, mutatis mutandis; provided that, prior to submitting a General Dispute Notice pursuant to Section 8.1(c)(ii) of the Separation Agreement, the Parties shall first comply with the procedures set forth in this Section 10.03. Pending final resolution of any Dispute, each Party shall continue performing its undisputed obligations under this Agreement and the applicable SLA. Provider shall not suspend, discontinue or reduce an Essential Site Service, or impair Recipient’s access to its Facility, solely by reason of the existence of a Dispute, and Recipient shall timely pay all undisputed amounts.

(b) Service-Specific Disputes. If a Dispute relates specifically to the provision, quality, scope or performance of a particular Service (a “Service-Specific Dispute”), such Service-Specific Dispute shall first be submitted in writing to the relevant Service Coordinator of each Party, and such Service Coordinators shall seek to resolve such Service-Specific Dispute through informal good faith negotiation. If such Service-Specific Dispute is not resolved by the relevant Service Coordinators within five (5) Business Days after submission to such Service Coordinators, the Service-Specific Dispute shall be escalated in writing to the Contract Manager of each Party, and such Contract Managers shall seek to resolve such Service-Specific Dispute through informal good faith negotiation within an additional five (5) Business Days.

 

B-31

(c) Non-Service-Specific Disputes. If a Dispute does not relate specifically to the provision, quality, scope or performance of a particular Service (a “Non-Service-Specific Dispute”), such Non-Service-Specific Dispute shall be submitted in writing directly to the Contract Manager of each Party, and such Contract Managers shall seek to resolve such Non-Service-Specific Dispute through informal good faith negotiation within ten (10) Business Days after submission to such Contract Managers.

(d) Extension of Time Periods. The Parties may agree in writing to extend any time period set forth in this Section 10.03.

(e) General Dispute Notice. If a Dispute is not resolved within the applicable period set forth above (as extended pursuant to Section 10.03(d), if applicable), then either Party may deliver a General Dispute Notice pursuant to Section 8.1(c)(ii) of the Separation Agreement and the terms and conditions of Article VIII of the Separation Agreement shall apply. Nothing in this Section 10.03 shall restrict either Party from seeking Interim Relief in accordance with Section 8.1(d)(viii) of the Separation Agreement.

ARTICLE XI

ENVIRONMENTAL, HEALTH AND SAFETY MATTERS

Section 11.01 Environmental, Health and Safety. In connection with the provision or receipt of Services hereunder or access to the Site under this Agreement, the following provisions shall apply:

(a) Permits; Shared Permits. Subject to the provisions of the Separation Agreement, and except as otherwise expressly provided in any SLA, each Party shall obtain and maintain, and comply with, the Permits required by applicable Law in connection with its provision or receipt of the Services (as applicable), or its access to the Site under this Agreement. If the Parties are operating under the same Permit in connection with any Service (a “Shared Permit”), each Party shall comply with the requirements of such Shared Permit applicable to its provision or receipt of the applicable Service and shall not knowingly take (or fail to take) any action in connection therewith that would prejudice the continuance or terms of the Shared Permit in any material respect. If a Shared Permit is only held in the name of one Party (the “Permit Holder”), the other Party shall comply with such Permit Holder’s reasonable instructions and provide such reasonable cooperation as such Permit Holder may reasonably request, in each case, to the extent necessary to comply with the terms of such Shared Permit. The Permit Holder shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain such Shared Permit to the extent necessary for the provision or receipt of a Service. Neither Party shall obtain, renew or modify any Permit in a manner that would reasonably be expected to materially and adversely affect the other Party’s provision or receipt of the Services without reasonable prior notice to (and consultation with) the other Party, except if required by applicable Law or a Governmental Entity.

 

B-32

(b) EHS Incidents. Except as otherwise expressly provided in any SLA, each Party shall notify the other Party in writing as promptly as practicable after becoming aware of a Release, material violation of Environmental Law or Permit, or other environmental, health, or safety incident, in each case arising from or relating to the provision or receipt of a Service (or access to the Site under this Agreement), that (i) is required to be reported or remediated under applicable Law or Permit or (ii) would reasonably be expected to materially affect such other Party (including its provision or receipt of a Service). Each Party shall take any and all corrective actions as required by applicable Law (or any Permit) with respect to the matters for which it is responsible under this Agreement, and shall reasonably cooperate with the other Party with respect thereto, including by providing such other Party with any material information or documentation reasonably requested thereby.

(c) Nothing in this Article XI shall alter or otherwise affect the allocation of environmental liabilities or responsibilities (including responsibility for any Remediation) under the Separation Agreement or Section 9.02 hereof, which shall control to the extent applicable.

ARTICLE XII

FORCE MAJEURE AND TEMPORARY SHUTDOWN

Section 12.01 Occurrence of Force Majeure.

(a) Excused Performance. A Party affected by a Force Majeure event shall be excused from (and shall not be liable for any failure or delay in) performance of its obligations under or pursuant to this Agreement only if, to the extent and for so long as performance of such obligations is prevented, materially delayed or materially hindered by such Force Majeure event. For the avoidance of doubt, a Force Majeure event shall not excuse payment of amounts that have accrued or are otherwise due for Services already provided. Recipient shall not be required to pay Service Fees and Expenses attributable to any portion of a Service not provided as a result of a Force Majeure event, except to the extent otherwise expressly provided in the applicable SLA.

(b) Notification and Mitigation. The affected Party shall notify the other Party as promptly as reasonably practicable after becoming aware of a Force Majeure event that would be reasonably expected to materially affect its performance hereunder, shall use commercially reasonable efforts to remedy or mitigate the effects thereof, including, where reasonably available, by implementing commercially reasonable temporary workarounds or alternative sources of supply, and shall resume performance as promptly as reasonably practicable. Nothing in this Section 12.01 shall be construed to require a Party to settle any labor dispute on terms it determines unacceptable.

(c) Temporary Substitute Services. Upon the occurrence and during the continuance of a Force Majeure event affecting Provider, Recipient shall be entitled to obtain, at its own expense, substitute services on a temporary basis. Provider shall, at Recipient’s reasonable request, provide reasonable cooperation, including reasonable access to those portions of the Site within Provider’s control as reasonably necessary in connection therewith. Recipient shall reimburse Provider for any reasonable, documented incremental out-of-pocket costs payable to Third Parties incurred by Provider in providing such cooperation. Any such access shall be subject to the applicable access and use requirements set forth in Sections 2.05(c) and (d).

 

B-33

(d) Prolonged Force Majeure. If a Force Majeure event continues for more than ninety (90) consecutive days or such shorter period as may be specified in the applicable SLA and, during such period, materially prevents the provision or receipt of any Service, either Party may terminate the affected Service upon thirty (30) days’ prior written notice to the other Party; provided that the Force Majeure event continues through the date of such termination. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Provider may terminate an Essential Site Service pursuant to this Section 12.01(d) only if (i) Recipient consents, (ii) a substitute service reasonably equivalent in all material respects is legally available and fully operational and, to the extent applicable, physically connected and tested, or (iii) both (A) continued performance of the affected Essential Site Service is unlawful or impossible and (B) no commercially reasonable lawful alternative is available despite Provider’s commercially reasonable efforts. Upon such termination, Provider shall have no further obligation to provide, and Recipient shall have no further obligation to accept, such Service, and all costs associated with such Service shall cease to accrue.

Section 12.02 Planned Temporary Shutdowns.

(a) Notice. If either Party anticipates a planned shutdown, maintenance activity or other planned outage at its applicable Facility, which is reasonably expected to materially interrupt or reduce its provision or receipt of a Service, such Party shall, to the extent reasonably practicable, provide the other Party with reasonable advance notice thereof, including as to the expected timing and duration (and shall promptly notify the other Party of any material changes to such information).

(b) Coordination and Restoration. The Parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to coordinate any planned shutdown, and the resumption of the applicable Service, in a safe and efficient manner, and so as to minimize any disruption to such Service. Following any planned shutdown or any unscheduled outage that materially impacts a Service, the Parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to restore such Service as promptly as practicable, subject to applicable Law, Permits and any emergency protocols then in effect and generally applicable at the Site.

Section 13.02 Successors and Assignment.

(a) Neither this Agreement nor any of the rights, interests or obligations under this Agreement shall be assigned or transferred, in whole or in part, by operation of Law or otherwise by either of the Parties without the prior written consent of the other Party (which consent may be granted or withheld in such other Party’s sole discretion); provided that either Party may assign or transfer, in whole or in part, by operation of Law or otherwise, without the prior written consent of the other Party, this Agreement or any of the rights, interests or obligations under this Agreement to (i) one or more of its Affiliates or (ii) the successor to all or a portion of the business or assets to which this Agreement relates; provided, further, that (A) the assigning or transferring Party shall promptly notify the non-assigning or non-transferring Party in writing of any assignment or transfer made under the foregoing clause (i) or clause (ii), (B) in the case of an assignment or transfer pursuant to either clause (i) or clause (ii), the Person to whom this Agreement is assigned or transferred shall agree in writing to be bound by the terms of this Agreement as if named as a “Party” hereto with respect to all or such portion of this Agreement so assigned or transferred, and (C) to the extent required by applicable Law for the provision or receipt of the applicable Services following such assignment or transfer, such Person shall hold or obtain the applicable Permits. Any purported assignment or transfer in violation of this Section 13.02 shall be void ab initio. No assignment or transfer shall relieve the assigning or transferring Party of any of its obligations under this Agreement that accrued prior to such assignment or transfer unless agreed to in writing by the non-assigning or non-transferring Party. With respect to any permitted assignment or transfer affecting an Essential Site Service, the assignee shall have the legal rights and Permits necessary to provide or receive the applicable Essential Site Service, as applicable, before such assignment or transfer becomes effective. Provider shall not voluntarily sell, transfer, lease, encumber or otherwise dispose of a Service Asset or access right necessary to an Essential Site Service in a manner reasonably expected to materially impair such Service unless commercially reasonable arrangements to preserve the applicable access and service rights are in effect before such disposition.

1.

BACKGROUND

This Service Level Agreement is entered into pursuant to the terms of the Site Services Agreement (Guad North), dated as of [•], 2026, by and between Provider and Recipient (the “Agreement”) and constitutes an SLA under the Agreement. Provider and Recipient, collectively with their permitted assigns, are referred to herein as the “Parties” and each, a “Party”. Capitalized terms used but not defined in this Service Level Agreement have the meanings assigned to those terms in the Agreement.

The Services provided under this Service Level Agreement are designated as Essential Site Services and Critical Services (each as defined in the Agreement). Without limiting any other provision of this Service Level Agreement or the Agreement, Provider shall not suspend, discontinue or reduce the Services, or impair Recipient’s access to its Facility, solely by reason of a Dispute, and the protections applicable to Essential Site Services under the Agreement shall apply to the Services.

Provider and Flextronics Technologies Mexico, S. de R.L. de C.V. (“Flextronics TM”) are parties to a certain Site Services Agreement, dated as of [•], and certain Service Level Agreement, dated as of [•] (collectively, the “FTM Agreement”), pursuant to which Provider provides electric and water distribution services to Flextronics TM. The Parties acknowledge and agree that certain shared infrastructure, capabilities, and services used to provide the Services are shared between Recipient under this Service Level Agreement and Flextronics TM under the FTM Agreement.

 

2.

ELECTRIC SERVICES DESCRIPTION

 

  A.

ELECTRIC SERVICES

 

  i.

Provider shall provide, and Recipient shall use and pay for, electric service for Recipient’s Facility, as agreed under this Service Level Agreement (the “Electric Services”). Subject to Section 2.B and Section 2.D, Provider shall supply the electricity requirements of Recipient’s Facility during the term of this Service Level Agreement up to the Guaranteed Power Capacity; in the understanding that Provider shall make commercially reasonable efforts to provide any capacity required by Recipient in excess of the Guaranteed Power Capacity as Additional Electric Services in accordance with Section 2.E. The Electric Services

 

B-43

  include the supply, allocation, delivery and distribution of electricity to Recipient’s individual buildings or properties through Provider’s private network within the Site, which electricity is supplied by the Comisión Federal de Electricidad (“CFE”). Any failure by Provider to deliver Electric Services to any individual property shall constitute a breach of this Service Level Agreement only if Provider fails to cure such failure within fifteen (15) Business Days after receiving written notice from Recipient; provided that Provider shall not be in breach to the extent the failure results from a Force Majeure Event, a Permitted Maintenance Outage, or the fault of a third party not under Provider’s reasonable control. Any breach under this paragraph shall be subject to the express remedies and limitations set forth in this Service Level Agreement and the Agreement.

 

  ii.

All capacity amounts stated in this Section 2 (including Section 2.E) and Schedule 1 (including the baseline of 19.5 MW, each increment under Scenario 1 or Scenario 2, and the resulting total of 29.5 MW) are aggregate amounts available jointly to Recipient under this Service Level Agreement and to Flextronics TM under the FTM Agreement, and are not cumulative. Schedule 1 shall set out the allocation of such aggregate amounts between this Service Level Agreement and the FTM Agreement, which allocation Recipient and Flextronics TM may reallocate between themselves by joint written notice to Provider, provided that the aggregate amount is not exceeded.

 

  B.

POWER RIGHTS

 

  i.

Provider shall reserve and make available to Recipient, from the Service Level Agreement Effective Date and throughout the term of this Service Level Agreement, a guaranteed minimum of 19.5 MW of electric capacity for Recipient’s operations, as may be increased from time to time in accordance with Section 2.B(ii) (the “Guaranteed Power Capacity”). The Guaranteed Power Capacity is a capacity amount (MW) available at any time, and not a measure of electricity consumed (kWh/MWh).

Recipient’s electricity consumption may fluctuate from month to month and may be below the Guaranteed Power Capacity. The Guaranteed Power Capacity is a reservation of capacity only and does not create any obligation for Recipient to consume the full Guaranteed Power Capacity in any month. Charges for the Electric Services shall be determined exclusively in accordance with Section 2.C and Section 2.E.

Provider shall have no obligation to supply electricity above the Guaranteed Power Capacity except as agreed under Section 2.E. As of the Service Level Agreement Effective Date, the Electric Services shall be supplied exclusively with electricity supplied by CFE. The source of electricity shall not limit or condition Provider’s obligation to make the Guaranteed Power Capacity available. Any source change requested by

 

B-44

Recipient that requires capital expenditures or new infrastructure shall be subject to Provider’s review and approval. The existing interchangeability arrangements for Recipient’s buildings shall be maintained, and any change to them shall require prior discussion between the Parties. Provider shall obtain and maintain the authorizations, permits and contracts necessary to deliver electricity from any source it uses and comply with applicable regulatory requirements for such purposes.

 

  ii.

Provider shall reserve and make available to Recipient electric capacity as set forth below, subject to the required governmental approvals and CFE delivery (any delay or failure of which shall constitute a Force Majeure Event). Each increment made available under paragraph (2) or (3) below, and any further increment agreed in writing under paragraph (4) below, shall form part of the Guaranteed Power Capacity from the date it is made available, with Schedule 1 to be updated accordingly.

 

  (1)

19.5 MW from the Service Level Agreement Effective Date, constituting the baseline Guaranteed Power Capacity under Section 2.B(i);

 

  (2)

if the approximately 40 MW capacity expansion at the Site is delivered as contemplated by the Parties (“Scenario 1”): (A) an additional 5 MW, to be made available to Recipient no later than January 31, 2027; (B) an additional 5 MW, to be made available to Recipient no later than October 31, 2027, resulting in a total Guaranteed Power Capacity of 29.5 MW; and (C) at Recipient’s option, an additional 10 MW, solely following delivery by CFE to Provider of an additional 150 MW; provided that if CFE is delayed in delivering such 150 MW but is able to deliver a portion of such amount, a proportional amount will be allocated to Recipient as it is made available;

 

  (3)

if Scenario 1 cannot be executed (“Scenario 2”): (A) an additional 3 MW, to be made available to Recipient no later than December 31, 2027, subject to CFE’s plan of record; and (B) an additional 7 MW, to be made available to Recipient no later than December 31, 2028, subject to CFE’s delivery of additional capacity to the Site; provided that, if CFE’s delivery is delayed, Recipient shall receive a proportional share of such additional capacity as it becomes available; and

 

  (4)

Recipient and Provider shall continue to negotiate in good faith Recipient’s incremental power capacity needs beyond the capacity set forth in this Section 2.B(ii).

 

  C.

COST

Recipient shall pay Provider for the Electric Services, including any Additional Electric Services, on the basis of the electricity actually consumed by Recipient’s Facility, as measured at the Dedicated Meters in kilowatt-hours (kWh). The rate per kWh shall be variable and calculated in accordance with Schedule 2. The rate shall be pass-through, without profit or margin for Provider, and shall not be expressed as a fixed amount.

 

B-45

If Provider and Recipient receive services from shared power infrastructure in the same building under a temporary cross-supply arrangement with a term of less than nine (9) months, the Parties will agree in writing, before any power is supplied under that arrangement, on how the costs of the shared power will be allocated between them.

 

  D.

EXCLUSIONS AND LIMITATIONS

The provision of Electric Services under this Service Level Agreement is subject to the following exclusions and limitations:

 

  i.

The Guaranteed Power Capacity in effect from time to time, including any increment under Section 2.B(ii), shall be reflected in Schedule 1 for planning and operational purposes. Except for increments made in accordance with Section 2.B(ii), changes to the Guaranteed Power Capacity shall require the mutual written agreement of the Parties.

 

  ii.

The Parties agree that the existing installed dedicated meters at the buildings leased by Recipient (“Dedicated Meters”) shall be utilized for measurement purposes. Provider shall be responsible for the maintenance, calibration, and replacement of the Dedicated Meters throughout the term of this Service Level Agreement. Recipient shall have the right to inspect the Dedicated Meters and request independent verification of their accuracy in accordance with Section 7.A.

 

  iii.

Provider does not guarantee uninterrupted or continuous Electric Services or redundancy of supply to the extent that any interruption results from a Force Majeure Event (including any failure of supply by CFE or equipment failure) or a Permitted Maintenance Outage. In such case, Provider’s obligation to make available the Guaranteed Power Capacity shall be excused for the duration of the applicable event; provided that Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to minimize the duration and impact of any such interruption and shall promptly notify Recipient of any emergency interruption. If commercially reasonable and subject to the Parties’ prior agreement on the applicable costs, the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to identify and, if agreed, obtain temporary alternative sources of power.

 

  iv.

The Parties acknowledge that the provision of Electric Services depends on Provider maintaining its continued status as an end-user under its supply agreement with CFE, the continued validity and effectiveness of Provider’s supply and connection agreements with CFE, and the continued existence, availability and operation of Provider’s private network within the Site. Provider shall be responsible for taking all reasonable actions within its control to maintain such status, agreements, permits, authorizations, capacity and private network, and any loss or impairment of the foregoing resulting from a Force Majeure Event shall be governed by Section 2.D(iii). Provider shall promptly notify Recipient of any communication, proceeding or action by CFE, or any other Governmental Entity that could reasonably be expected to affect the Electric Services.

 

B-46

  v.

Provider shall not enter into any agreement, commitment, or arrangement with any third party that would reduce the amount of electricity available to Recipient below the Guaranteed Power Capacity, without Recipient’s prior written consent; provided that Provider may enter into arrangements with third parties for surplus electric capacity above the Guaranteed Power Capacity, so long as such arrangements do not reduce availability to Recipient below the Guaranteed Power Capacity. For purposes of this Section 2.D(v), Flextronics TM shall not be considered a third party with respect to the aggregate capacity allocated under Section 2.B.

 

  vi.

If the source of electricity used to provide the Electric Services changes in the future, the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to negotiate and agree upon any amendments to this Service Level Agreement that may be necessary to reflect such change, provided that all applicable legal and technical requirements under Mexican Law for the supply of electricity from such alternative source have been satisfied and that any such requirements, to the extent applicable to the implementation of such change, shall be expressly incorporated into the relevant amendment to this Service Level Agreement.

 

  E.

ADDITIONAL ELECTRIC SERVICES AND FORECASTING

Recipient may request in writing that Provider provide electric capacity in excess of the Guaranteed Power Capacity (“Additional Electric Services”). Each request for Additional Electric Services (a “Power Capacity Request”) must specify the amount and duration of capacity requested and include: (a) Recipient’s good-faith forecasts of its power requirements for the short term (the next twelve (12) months), the medium term (the next twelve (12) to thirty-six (36) months), and the long term (more than thirty-six (36) months); and (b) any supporting documentation Provider reasonably requests to evaluate the Power Capacity Request, including customer load profiles, production schedules, and equipment specifications. Provider shall respond in writing to each Power Capacity Request within five (5) Business Days of receipt.

 

  i.

Availability; Provider Priority. Any provision of Additional Electric Services depends on Provider determining, in its sole discretion, that it has power capacity, capital expenditure budget and supporting infrastructure available after meeting Provider’s own current and projected requirements (“Excess Power Capacity”).

 

  ii.

Methods of Provision. If Excess Power Capacity is available and the Parties sign a written agreement on the amount of Additional Electric Services and its terms, Provider will make it available to Recipient by one of the following methods:

(a) Temporary Allocation. Provider allocates the Additional Electric Services to Recipient for an initial term of one (1) year. Before each anniversary of the start of that

 

B-47

term, the Parties will reassess whether Recipient still needs the Additional Electric Services, based on Recipient’s updated forecasts. Provider may choose, in its sole discretion, not to renew the allocation for any following one (1)-year term by giving Recipient written notice at least ninety (90) days before the current term ends. The Parties will revise the allocation of fees for any renewal term to reflect the Additional Electric Services being allocated. A temporary allocation shall not increase the Guaranteed Power Capacity.

(b) Permanent Incremental Allocation. The Parties may agree that Provider permanently allocates the Additional Electric Services to Recipient, in which case Recipient will pay all costs of any capital expenditure (including but not limited to hardware and mechanical and electrical equipment) needed to deliver it, and such Additional Electric Services shall form part of the Guaranteed Power Capacity.

(c) Dedicated Expansion. Provider expands its capital assets and infrastructure to create the Additional Electric Services, and Recipient pays all of the costs of such expansion. The resulting Additional Electric Services will be dedicated to Recipient’s exclusive use, under the terms the Parties agree in writing, and shall form part of the Guaranteed Power Capacity.

If the Parties agree in writing that Provider will pursue additional capacity in order to provide Additional Electric Services, Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to pursue the required procedures with CFE and any other competent Governmental Entity and keep Recipient reasonably informed and provide Recipient with copies of any material communications with CFE or any other Governmental Entity relating thereto. Provider shall not be liable for any delay, refusal or inability caused solely by any Governmental Entity, provided that Provider has timely taken the actions within its control and continues to diligently pursue the requested capacity.

Additional Electric Services shall be charged in accordance with the pricing mechanism under Section 2.C, together with any costs agreed by the Parties in writing under this Section 2.E (including approved capital expenditures and any revised allocation of fees for a temporary allocation). Provider shall not charge Recipient any profit or margin in respect of the Electric Services.

 

3.

WATER DISTRIBUTION SERVICES DESCRIPTION

 

  A.

SERVICES

Provider, as the lawful holder of one or more water concession(s) granted by the National Water Commission (Comisión Nacional del Agua, “CONAGUA”) in accordance with the National Waters Act (Ley de Aguas Nacionales), its Regulations (Reglamento de la Ley de Aguas Nacionales), and all other applicable Mexican Law, shall provide the allocation, distribution and delivery of water service through Provider’s private existing infrastructure to the properties, buildings, and facilities that comprise the Recipient’s Facility, up to the Baseline Water Allocation (the “Water Distribution Services”, and together with the Electric Services, the “Services”) during the term of this Service Level Agreement, subject to the exclusions and limitations in Section 3.C; in the understanding that Provider shall make commercially reasonable efforts to provide any water distribution services required by Recipient in excess of the

 

B-48

Baseline Water Allocation as Additional Water Distribution Services in accordance with Section 3.D. Provider shall obtain and maintain the permits, authorizations, concessions, and registrations required under applicable Mexican Law to provide the Water Distribution Services and operate the infrastructure necessary for the allocation, distribution and delivery of water volumes required hereunder to Recipient’s Facility, subject to Section 3.C(ii).

The Baseline Water Allocation is an aggregate amount available jointly to Recipient under this Service Level Agreement and to Flextronics TM under the FTM Agreement, and is not cumulative. Schedule 3 shall set out the allocation of such aggregate amount between this Service Level Agreement and the FTM Agreement, and among such entities, which allocation Recipient and Flextronics TM may reallocate between themselves by joint written notice to Provider, provided that the aggregate amount is not exceeded.

Subject to Section 3.C, Provider shall deliver water to Recipient’s individual properties within the Site, in the volumes (up to the Baseline Water Allocation), quality standards, and pressure levels reasonably required for the operation of Recipient’s activities during the term of this Service Level Agreement. Any failure by Provider to deliver water to an individual property shall constitute a breach of this Service Level Agreement only if Provider fails to cure such failure within fifteen (15) Business Days after receiving written notice from Recipient; provided that Provider shall not be in breach to the extent the failure results from a Force Majeure Event, a Permitted Maintenance Outage, an act or omission of CONAGUA or any other Governmental Entity, or the fault of a third party not under Provider’s reasonable control. Any breach under this paragraph shall be subject to the express remedies and limitations set forth in this Service Level Agreement and the Agreement.

The Parties acknowledge that: (i) water is a national asset (bien nacional) whose ownership corresponds to the Mexican Nation pursuant to Article 27 of the Political Constitution of the United Mexican States (Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos) and the National Waters Act; (ii) the Water Distribution Services constitute exclusively a service for the allocation, distribution, and physical delivery of water and do not constitute, nor shall they be construed as, a sale, transfer, conveyance, or assignment of water as a commodity or of any water rights; and (iii) the Water Distribution Services include the allocation, distribution, and delivery of water through Provider’s private existing infrastructure and any extensions, improvements, or additions thereto that may be required to ensure delivery to each of Recipient’s facilities, all under Provider’s water concession(s).

The Parties further acknowledge that the water distributed under this Service Level Agreement is supplied under Provider’s water concession(s) from groundwater extracted by Provider through wells located within the Site (currently three (3)) (the “Water Source”). Provider shall obtain and maintain the permits and authorizations required under applicable Mexican Law to receive and distribute water from the Water Source.

 

B-49

  B.

COST

Recipient shall pay Provider for the Water Distribution Services, including any Additional Water Distribution Service, on the basis of the volume of water actually distributed to Recipient’s facilities, as measured in cubic meters (m³) at the applicable meters (or if meters are not available, on the basis otherwise agreed by the Parties) (the “Water Distribution Fee”). Such fees constitute compensation for the operation, maintenance, administration, and provision of Provider’s water distribution infrastructure, including pumping, treatment, and metering systems, and do not constitute, nor shall they be construed as, a price, payment, or consideration for the sale, transfer, or assignment of water or any water rights. For the avoidance of doubt, the Water Distribution Fee does not include any component attributable to the intrinsic value of the water distributed, which remains a national asset (bien nacional) not subject to private appropriation. The rate per cubic meter (m³) shall be variable and calculated in accordance with Schedule 4. The rate shall be pass-through, without profit or margin for Provider, consistent with the arm’s-length principle and applicable Mexican Law.

 

  C.

EXCLUSIONS AND LIMITATIONS

The provision of Water Distribution Services under this Service Level Agreement is subject to the following exclusions and limitations:

 

  i.

Provider shall reserve and make available to Recipient the volume of water set forth in Schedule 3 (the “Baseline Water Allocation”). The Baseline Water Allocation shall constitute the maximum volume that Provider is obligated to distribute to Recipient’s facilities; provided that Provider shall also distribute any Additional Water Distribution Services agreed under Section 3.D. Changes to the Baseline Water Allocation shall require the mutual written agreement of the Parties; provided, however, that Provider shall not reduce the Baseline Water Allocation without Recipient’s prior written consent.

 

  ii.

The Water Distribution Services are subject to the terms, conditions, and volume limitations of Provider’s water concession(s) granted by CONAGUA. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain its water concession(s) in good standing and to pursue renewal and, where commercially reasonable, expansion of the volumetric allocation thereunder. Provider shall promptly notify Recipient of any communication, proceeding, or action by CONAGUA or any other Governmental Entity that could reasonably be expected to affect the Water Distribution Services, including any reduction, modification, suspension, or revocation of Provider’s water concession(s). Provider shall not be liable for any delay, reduction or inability to obtain or maintain concession volume caused by CONAGUA, another Governmental Entity, or a third party beyond Provider’s reasonable control.

 

  iii.

The Parties acknowledge that the water infrastructure within the Site consists of two (2) categories: (a) the infrastructure that, as holder of the water concession title(s), Provider is required to install under applicable Mexican Law to extract water through wells when the source is groundwater, including a meter installed at the point of extraction to measure the volumes consumed, which meter is connected to CONAGUA and transmits daily consumption measurements (the

 

B-50

  “Concession Infrastructure”); and (b) any infrastructure constructed downstream of such metering point, which is considered additional infrastructure and is privately owned (the “Additional Infrastructure”). The Additional Infrastructure used for the distribution of water volumes supplied by Provider to Recipient shall be independent from and separate from the Concession Infrastructure associated with Provider’s concession titles for the use and exploitation of national waters within the Site. Provider shall maintain such separation in compliance with applicable Mexican Law and shall ensure that such separation does not adversely affect Recipient’s right to receive the Water Distribution Services or the Additional Water Distribution Services contemplated under Section 3.D. Provider shall be solely responsible for obtaining and maintaining all environmental permits, licenses, and authorizations required for the operation of the Concession Infrastructure and the Additional Infrastructure used for the provision of the Water Distribution Services.

 

  iv.

In the event that CONAGUA reduces, modifies, suspends, or revokes Provider’s water concession(s), or if the available volume under such concession(s) is or may become insufficient to fully satisfy the Baseline Water Allocation, Provider shall: (a) notify Recipient in writing within five (5) Business Days of becoming aware of such event; (b) prioritize the allocation of available water volume to Recipient’s facilities before allocating water to third parties; (c) use commercially reasonable efforts to cooperate with Recipient in good faith to identify and implement commercially reasonable alternatives, including seeking additional concession volume from CONAGUA or securing alternative water supply sources; and (d) the Parties shall equitably share the reasonable, documented incremental costs associated with securing such alternative supply, taking into account the relative benefits, control and responsibility of the Parties; provided that, to the extent such event results from Provider’s breach of this Service Level Agreement or failure to maintain its water concession(s) in good standing, such costs shall be borne by Provider. Provider shall not be required to incur material capital expenditures for alternative supply unless Recipient has approved such expenditures in writing and agreed to bear its agreed share of the costs.

 

  v.

Provider’s obligation to provide the Water Distribution Services shall be limited to the distribution of the water volumes required under this Service Level Agreement to Recipient through Provider’s private infrastructure within the Site and all actions reasonably necessary to maintain such private infrastructure in proper operating condition and with sufficient capacity to enable Provider to perform its obligations under this Service Level Agreement.

 

  vi.

Provider shall not enter into any agreement, commitment, or arrangement with any third party that would reduce the volume of water available for distribution to Recipient below the Baseline Water Allocation, without Recipient’s prior written consent; provided that Provider may enter into arrangements with third parties for surplus water capacity above the Baseline Water Allocation, so long as such arrangements do not reduce availability to Recipient below the Baseline Water Allocation.

 

B-51

  vii.

A portion of the Baseline Water Allocation will be distributed by Provider to Recipient for use in Recipient’s chilled water system (the “Chilled Water Supply”); provided that in addition to being supplied from the Water Source, it may also be supplied from other sources to be agreed between the Parties.

 

  viii.

Any future investments, capital expenditures, expansions, or improvements made by or on behalf of Provider in the Concession Infrastructure or the Additional Infrastructure for purposes of Provider’s own growth or the growth of its other operations within the Site shall be borne solely by Provider and shall not be charged to Recipient, whether as part of the Water Distribution Fee or otherwise.

 

  ix.

Each Party shall have the right, at any time and independently, to contract for the supply of water directly with the Governmental Entity having jurisdiction over the Site or with any third party duly authorized by such Governmental Entity for such purpose, in accordance with applicable Mexican Law. Any such contracting shall be at the sole cost, expense, and responsibility of the contracting Party, and shall not modify, reduce, or otherwise affect the other Party’s rights and obligations under this Service Level Agreement, including Provider’s obligation to make available the Baseline Water Allocation.

 

  D.

ADDITIONAL WATER DISTRIBUTION SERVICES AND FORECASTING

Recipient may request in writing that Provider provide water distribution services (including for the Chilled Water Supply) in excess of the Baseline Water Allocation (“Additional Water Distribution Services”). Each request for Additional Water Distribution Services (a “Water Capacity Request”) must specify the volume, duration, and the specific facilities requiring such additional services and include: (a) Recipient’s good-faith forecasts of its water distribution requirements for the short term (the next twelve (12) months), the medium term (the next twelve (12) to thirty-six (36) months), and the long term (more than thirty-six (36) months); and (b) any supporting documentation Provider reasonably requests to evaluate the Water Capacity Request, including equipment specifications. Provider shall respond in writing to each such Water Capacity Request within five (5) Business Days of receipt.

 

  i.

Availability; Provider Priority. Any provision of Additional Water Distribution Service depends on Provider determining, in its sole discretion, that it has available volume from the Water Source or other applicable source and supporting infrastructure available after meeting Provider’s own current and projected requirements (“Excess Water Capacity”).

 

B-52

  ii.

Methods of Provision. If Excess Water Capacity is available and the Parties sign a written agreement on the amount of Additional Water Distribution Service and its terms, Provider will make it available to Recipient by one of the following methods:

(a) Temporary Allocation. Provider allocates the Additional Water Distribution Service to Recipient for an initial term of one (1) year. Before each anniversary of the start of that term, the Parties will reassess whether Recipient still needs the Additional Water Distribution Service, based on Recipient’s updated forecasts. Provider may choose, in its sole discretion, not to renew the allocation for any following one (1)-year term by giving Recipient written notice at least ninety (90) days before the current term ends. The Parties will revise the allocation of fees for any renewal term to reflect the Additional Water Distribution Service being allocated. A temporary allocation shall not increase the Baseline Water Allocation.

(b) Permanent Incremental Allocation. The Parties may agree that Provider permanently allocates the Additional Water Distribution Service to Recipient, in which case Recipient will pay all costs of any capital expenditure (including but not limited to hardware and mechanical and electrical equipment) needed to deliver it, and such Additional Water Distribution Service shall form part of the Baseline Water Allocation.

(c) Dedicated Expansion. Provider expands its capital infrastructure to create the Additional Water Distribution Service, and Recipient pays all of the costs of such expansion. The resulting Additional Water Distribution Service will be dedicated to Recipient’s exclusive use, under the terms the Parties agree in writing, and shall form part of the Baseline Water Allocation.

If the Parties agree in writing that Provider will pursue additional water volumes in order to provide Additional Water Distribution Service, Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to pursue the required procedures with CONAGUA and keep Recipient reasonably informed and provide Recipient with copies of any material communications with CONAGUA relating thereto. Provider shall not be liable for any delay, refusal or inability caused solely by any Governmental Entity, provided that Provider has timely taken the actions within its control and continues to diligently pursue the requested capacity.

Additional Water Distribution Service shall be charged in accordance with the pricing mechanism under Section 3.B, together with any costs agreed by the Parties in writing under this Section 3.D. Provider shall not charge Recipient any profit or margin in respect of Water Distribution Services.

 

4.

ADDITIONAL CONSIDERATION

 

  A.

GENERAL PRINCIPLES

It is the intent of Provider and Recipient that the cost calculations in this Service Level Agreement will capture all costs, fees and credits incurred by Provider associated with the delivery of the Services to Recipient without subsidizing Recipient or unduly benefitting Provider. Although Provider and Recipient have attempted to anticipate all of the costs associated with the delivery of the Services over the term of this Service Level Agreement, any unforeseen costs directly associated with the delivery of the Services will be passed on to Recipient. To the

 

B-53

extent Provider incurs a cost in connection with the delivery of a Service that benefits Recipient, such cost will be shared with Recipient. To the extent Provider reduces a cost in connection with the delivery of a Service that benefits Recipient, such cost savings will also be shared with Recipient. Recipient shall have the right, upon reasonable notice, to review Provider’s books and records supporting any costs charged under this Service Level Agreement.

Costs will be determined using Provider’s accounting rules on the Service Level Agreement Effective Date. Any proposed changes to such accounting rules (and the financial impact of such changes) will be disclosed to Recipient in advance.

 

  B.

INCREMENTAL SUPPORT COSTS

Recipient shall be solely responsible for all costs, fees, charges or expenses relating to or resulting from the Services requested by Recipient where Recipient is the primary beneficiary (to the extent any such costs, fees, charges or expenses have not already been charged to Recipient hereunder), including any incremental costs of complying with applicable Mexican Law or obtaining or modifying Permits to the extent arising solely from such requested Services.

 

5.

TERM AND TERMINATION

 

  A.

TERM

This Service Level Agreement is effective as of the Service Level Agreement Effective Date and shall continue in effect for the duration of the term of the Guadalajara Lease, which may be extended for an additional period upon terms to be agreed by the Parties, unless terminated in accordance with this Service Level Agreement or the Agreement.

 

  B.

TERMINATION

 

  i.

Except as expressly provided in Section 5.B(iii), Section 5.B(iv) and Section 6, Provider shall have no right to voluntarily terminate this Service Level Agreement or any Service under this Service Level Agreement unless Recipient has expressly consented in writing and materially equivalent substitute services are legally available, physically connected, tested and fully operational for Recipient.

 

  ii.

Recipient may terminate any Service by giving Provider written notice that satisfies the Required Notice Period applicable to Recipient for such Service.

 

  iii.

Provider may terminate a Service if Recipient has permanently ceased using that Service or fails to pay undisputed amounts due for that Service for a period of six (6) months and does not cure such failure within thirty (30) days after written notice, in each case subject to the Essential Site Services protections of this Service Level Agreement and the Agreement.

 

B-54

  iv.

Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in the Agreement, if at any time, any Governmental Entity threatens to initiate or initiates any action claiming or asserting jurisdiction over Provider as a public utility or electric utility due to Provider’s provision of the Services, the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to identify and implement a commercially reasonable solution that permits the Services to continue in compliance with applicable Mexican Law before either Party may seek termination on that basis. Provider shall not terminate this Service Level Agreement solely because of any such threat or action unless the Parties have exhausted such good-faith cooperation and no legally permissible solution is available.

 

6.

CHANGE IN LAW

“Change in Law” shall mean the occurrence, after the Service Level Agreement Effective Date, of any of the following: (i) the adoption, publication, or taking effect of any Law, rule, code, Mexican official standards, regulation or treaty; (ii) any change in any Law, rule, regulation, code, Mexican official standards, order, decree or treaty, including any amendment or modification to the Energy Sector and Water Law, its regulations, or any rules, guidelines or criteria issued by the Ministry of Energy (“SENER”), CONAGUA or the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources (“SEMARNAT”); or in the administration, interpretation, implementation or application thereof by any Governmental Entity, including any change affecting private network requirements, water concession terms, water quality standards, environmental permits, or the terms and conditions of supply and connection agreements with CFE; or (iii) the making or issuance of any request, guideline, resolution or directive (whether or not having the force of law) by any Governmental Entity, including SEMARNAT, CONAGUA, CFE and SENER.

If a Change in Law occurs which (i) renders it impossible or unlawful for Provider to perform or otherwise give effect to any material obligation under this Service Level Agreement; (ii) causes any material provisions of this Service Level Agreement to become inconsistent with applicable Mexican Law; (iii) materially and adversely affects the regulatory approvals, permits, or agreements upon which the provision of the Services depends, including the supply and connection agreements with CFE or the authorization to operate a private network within the Site; or (iv) materially and adversely affects Provider’s water concession titles, environmental permits, or authorizations required for the extraction, distribution, or discharge of water, or imposes new or more restrictive water quality, volumetric, or environmental standards affecting the Water Distribution Services (each, a “Relevant Change in Law”), then a Party may give notice to the other Party of the Relevant Change in Law occurring. The Parties shall meet within fifteen (15) Business Days of such notice to negotiate in good faith such amendments to this Service Level Agreement as are necessary to (A) ensure that Recipient can continue to receive the Services as promptly as possible and with minimal service interruption; (B) achieve (so far as is possible) the same overall balance of rights, obligations, liabilities, risks, and costs under this Service Level Agreement as applied immediately prior to the Relevant Change in Law and to ensure that performance of this Service Level Agreement remains legal and enforceable; (C) allocate fairly between the Parties the incremental costs, if any, of implementing such amendments or restructuring the manner in which the Services are provided; and (D) ensure that any change in the manner of providing the Water Distribution Services continues to comply with the principle that Recipient is charged solely for the distribution service and not for the water itself.

 

B-55

For the avoidance of doubt, a Change in Law shall not, in and of itself, excuse Provider from its obligation to provide the Services or entitle Provider to suspend, curtail or terminate the Services, except to the extent performance becomes unlawful or impossible. The Parties shall cooperate in good faith to identify and implement commercially reasonable changes to the manner or method of providing the Services that are necessary to allow the Services to continue to be provided in compliance with applicable Mexican Law, including by pursuing any amendments to governmental permits, registrations, water concessions, environmental authorizations, or agreements that may be required. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith an equitable allocation of the incremental costs of complying with a Change in Law or implementing such changes. If the Parties are unable to agree on such cost allocation or amendments within ninety (90) days following delivery of notice of a Relevant Change in Law, Recipient may terminate this Service Level Agreement upon sixty (60) days’ prior written notice to Provider, and Provider may terminate this Service Level Agreement only if performance of the Services has become unlawful or impossible and no legally permissible solution is available. In either case, the Parties shall continue to cooperate to provide and receive the Services until the later of the end of such notice period and the date on which materially equivalent substitute services are available to Recipient, in each case, to the extent legally permissible.

 

7.

OTHER TERMS

 

  A.

EQUIPMENT

Provider shall own, operate, maintain and provide telemetry for the metering and distribution equipment for purposes of providing the Services, unless otherwise agreed by the Parties. Recipient shall have the right to inspect any such equipment upon reasonable prior notice and subject to applicable Site safety rules. Provider shall ensure that metering equipment is calibrated and certified in accordance with applicable Mexican Law and industry standards. Recipient shall have the right to request independent verification of metering accuracy and water quality testing results at Recipient’s cost (or at Provider’s cost if the metering equipment is found to be outside applicable tolerances, in which case charges shall be adjusted for the period of inaccuracy), provided such request shall not be made more than once per calendar year. If any Dedicated Meter or other meter used to measure the Services is unavailable, malfunctioning or not yet installed for any period, consumption of the applicable Service for such period shall be allocated on a reasonable basis, taking into account Recipient’s historical usage and any other available information, subject to a true-up once accurate meter readings are available.

 

  B.

GENERAL LIMITATIONS

The Services do not include any service, facility or obligation not expressly described in this Service Level Agreement or the Schedules, except as otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties.

The Parties agree that natural gas supply is not covered by this Service Level Agreement.

 

B-56

Provider shall be responsible for environmental liability arising from the operation of the water distribution infrastructure, including any contamination, spill, or unauthorized discharge occurring within Provider’s distribution network, except to the extent resulting from pre-existing contamination or contamination caused by Recipient’s operations or activities.

 

  C.

DISRUPTIONS AND MAINTENANCE

Recipient shall ensure that Recipient’s facilities are able to safely shut down in the event of a complete loss of electric service, whatever its source.

The Parties shall use commercially reasonable efforts to coordinate planned maintenance and restore Services as promptly as practicable following any disruption, subject to applicable Mexican Law, Permits and emergency protocols applicable at the Site. Provider shall provide Recipient with not less than ninety (90) days’ prior written notice of any planned maintenance that may materially affect the provision of the Services, except in the case of emergency maintenance, in which case Provider shall provide notice as soon as reasonably practicable. Provider shall use commercially reasonable efforts to schedule planned maintenance during periods of low demand and to minimize disruption to Recipient’s operations.

Interruptions of the Services during planned maintenance notified in accordance with this Section 7.C or during emergency maintenance notified as soon as reasonably practicable in accordance with this Section 7.C (each, a “Permitted Maintenance Outage”) shall not constitute a breach of this Service Level Agreement.

 

  D.

REGULATORY CONSIDERATIONS

The Parties acknowledge and agree that it is not the intent of the Parties for Provider to be regulated as a public utility, electric utility or similar entity under Mexican Law. No undertaking by Provider in this Service Level Agreement will constitute the dedication of Provider’s interconnection and distribution facilities or any related portion to the public. Provider is not a public utility or electric utility and Provider’s provision of the Services under this Service Level Agreement is expressly contingent upon the continued operation of Provider’s electricity supply and distribution facilities free from regulation as a public utility or electric utility, in any respect whatsoever under any applicable Mexican Law.

The Parties further acknowledge that the Water Distribution Services are provided under and subject to Provider’s water concession(s) granted by CONAGUA and do not constitute the provision of a public water supply service. Nothing in this Service Level Agreement shall be construed as authorizing Provider to act as a public water utility or to provide water supply services to third parties outside the Site without the appropriate governmental authorizations.

To the extent the Parties are affiliates, the pricing for the Services shall be determined on an arm’s-length basis and shall comply with applicable transfer pricing rules under Mexican Law.

 

B-57

  E.

CONTRACT ADMINISTRATOR

Each Party shall provide the other with written notice informing such Party of the applicable contract administrator contact information. Either Party may change its contract administrator contact information by providing written notice to the other Party of such change. Any change in contract administrator contact information is effective upon delivery of such written notice to the other Party. Either Party may elect to have one notice of contract administrator contact information govern multiple Service Level Agreements.

 

  F.

INFRASTRUCTURE OWNERSHIP

The Parties acknowledge that Provider owns the electrical and water distribution infrastructure and facilities within the Site, including all substations, transformers, distribution lines, meters, pipes, valves, pumping stations, storage tanks and related equipment used for the provision of the Services. Provider shall be responsible for routine maintenance, ordinary repairs, and replacement of its distribution infrastructure necessary for such infrastructure to function properly. Any upgrade that primarily benefits Recipient, including a capacity expansion requested by Recipient, shall be subject to Recipient’s prior written approval and equitable cost-sharing as agreed by the Parties; provided that Recipient shall not be responsible for replacements or capital expenditures required for Provider’s infrastructure to function or to maintain the Guaranteed Power Capacity. Recipient shall not make any modifications or connections to the distribution infrastructure without Provider’s prior written consent. The ownership, maintenance and replacement obligations with respect to the distribution infrastructure may also be addressed in the Guadalajara Lease between the Parties, and in the event of any conflict, the terms of the Guadalajara Lease shall prevail; provided that nothing in the Guadalajara Lease shall reduce Provider’s obligations under this Service Level Agreement with respect to the Guaranteed Power Capacity, the Baseline Water Allocation or the provision of the Services.

 

8.

MISCELLANEOUS

This Service Level Agreement is incorporated by reference into the Agreement. In the event of any conflict between the terms of this Service Level Agreement and the Agreement, the terms of this Service Level Agreement shall prevail. This Service Level Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of Mexico, consistent with the governing law of the Agreement. Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Service Level Agreement, including any question regarding its existence, validity, interpretation, performance, breach, or termination, shall be finally resolved by binding arbitration in accordance with the Rules of Arbitration of the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC), as in effect from time to time. The seat of arbitration shall be Mexico City, Mexico. The arbitration proceedings shall be conducted in the English language, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties. The arbitral tribunal shall consist of three arbitrators, appointed in accordance with the ICC Rules. The award rendered by the arbitral tribunal shall be final and binding upon the Parties.

 

B-58

Except for liability arising from a Party’s fraud, willful misconduct or gross negligence, each Party’s total aggregate liability under this Service Level Agreement, whether in contract, statute or otherwise, shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable by Recipient under this Service Level Agreement during the twenty-four (24)-month period preceding the event giving rise to the claim. This limitation shall apply notwithstanding any other provision of this Service Level Agreement or the Agreement, except to the extent a specific provision expressly provides a lower limitation or an exclusive remedy.
